#3330. IEEE Offers More Services to Cities That Want to Be Smarter

The November issue of IEEE Spectrum is here!

They include webinars, educational resources, and conferences

Georges Zissis is an IEEE Fellow and chair of the IEEE Smart Cities Technical Community.

Satish Sani is an IEEE senior member and chair of the IEEE Smart Grid Technical Track.

More and more city governments are using advanced technologies to improve livability for their residents. Municipalities use data from smartphones and sensors for traffic enforcement, traffic control, and waste management. They also have implemented artificial intelligence and deep learning programs.

Dubai, Paris, and Coral Gables, Fla., are among the cities that have invested heavily in programs to become smarter.

Although many initiatives have delivered real innovations, not all have been successful. Inefficient global coordination has hindered projects with unclear standards, socioeconomic differences, and a lack of worldwide governance, leading to a disconnect between the technologies and the ability to adapt to them.

Smart city projects are complex and expensive endeavors that involve politicians, citizens, technocrats, and engineers. Successful projects require citizens to be fully engaged and to have strong collaborations with the participants, especially engineers, as engineering is the cornerstone.

Collaboration with universities, research institutions, and technology experts can bridge knowledge gaps on the behavior of complex socio-technical systems. What’s missing, though, is a global platform where those involved can discuss their experiences.

To help solve those and other challenges, the IEEE Smart Cities Technical Community (formerly the IEEE Smart Cities Initiative) was launched in 2013 by IEEE Future Directions, which incubates emerging technologies and new applications of current ones. The technical community provides city leaders and others with credible, unbiased information and educational content developed by IEEE experts.

Since then, IEEE Smart Cities has launched services including its flagship International Smart Cities Conference, a media center with educational and technical resources, and a contest to recognize the best smart project completed by city officials. The platforms bring together practicing engineers, academic researchers, policymakers, and city leaders to collaborate and exchange ideas and experiences about moving toward a smart-city model.

In 2021 the IEEE Power & Energy Society began managing the Smart Cities program, which is supported by the IEEE Communications, Industry Applications, and Intelligent Transportation Systems societies and other IEEE entities.

Thanks to volunteers’ dedication and determination, IEEE Smart Cities launched several services. But the initiative’s structure limited the development of long-term projects and the creation of new activities.

To address the situation, the IEEE Technical Activities Board (TAB) created the second-generation technical community ad hoc committee, also in 2021. It was a pilot program whereby IEEE Smart Cities formed a board of governors to oversee the community’s operations and leadership, and created a policies and procedures manual.

In November 2025 IEEE Smart Cities became a TAB technical community.

Today more than 7,000 volunteers collaborate on various aspects of the community within at least one of the following technical tracks:

New webinar series, workshops, conferences, educational resources, and other offerings are being created.

Two events were launched recently: the IEEE European Technology and Engineering Management Summit, held in May 2025 in Belgium, with the next one planned for 2027; and the IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference, scheduled for 2 to 6 December in Athens.

The Smart Cities Ambassadors program aims to raise the technical community’s visibility outside IEEE by holding roundtables and other events at non-IEEE functions.

IEEE Smart Cities volunteers are working on launching journals. In addition, standards are being developed in collaboration with the IEEE Standards Association, societies, and councils.

The program is collaborating with the Open and Agile Smart Cities and Communities network, the Instituto de Competitividad e Innovación para el Desarrollo y Transferencia de Tecnología, and the International Project Management Association.

All of those actions have the ultimate objective of boosting IEEE Smart Cities’ growth and sustainability, as well as strengthening the leadership and educational offerings to technical community volunteers.

If you would like to volunteer, visit the Smart Cities website.

Georges Zissis is an IEEE Fellow and chair of the IEEE Smart Cities Technical Community.

Satish Sani is an IEEE senior member and chair of the IEEE Smart Grid Technical Track.

The Christmas countdown is officially underway, and if you’re anything like me, a few festive movies and shows are essential for getting into the holiday spirit. Thankfully, Netflix is making it easier to get started, with the streaming service adding a fresh batch of Christmas movies throughout November. Whether you’re ready for cozy festive romances, family-friendly adventures or something a little different to break up the usual holiday viewing, there’s plenty to watch.

With new originals joining some overlooked Christmas gems, this month’s lineup has a little something for different tastes. It’s also a good excuse to revisit your festive watchlist and discover a few new favorites before December rolls around. I’ve picked out five Christmas movies and shows I’d recommend checking out first, so you can get your holiday viewing off to a good start.

“The Best Christmas Pageant Ever” is a charming comedy-drama based on Barbara Robinson’s much-loved 1972 children’s novel. Directed by Dallas Jenkins, best known for creating the hit series “The Chosen,” the movie was a passion project more than 15 years in the making, with Jenkins describing the book as an important part of his childhood. Released in November 2024, it earned positive reviews from critics and audiences, with Judy Greer and Beatrice Schneider among the standout performers. It’s a lovely choice for a family movie night.

Six unruly siblings known as the Herdmans have a reputation for causing trouble wherever they go. When they turn up at the local church looking for free snacks, they end up volunteering for the annual Christmas pageant and landing all the leading roles. Grace Bradley (Judy Greer), who has taken over directing the production for the first time, is left scrambling to prepare the children for their big performance. With the Herdmans unfamiliar with the Christmas story and the rest of the town convinced the show will be a disaster, rehearsals quickly become unpredictable.

“No Sleep ’Til Christmas” is a cozy holiday rom-com that first premiered on Freeform as part of its annual “25 Days of Christmas” lineup. The movie puts a fun spin on the festive formula with a quirky premise centred on two strangers struggling with severe insomnia who discover they can only fall asleep when they’re together. Dave Annable and Odette Annable lead the cast, and their real-life marriage brings an easy chemistry to the central relationship. It’s a lighthearted pick if you’re after a feel-good Christmas movie with a slightly unusual twist.

Lizzie (Odette Annable) is a successful event planner struggling with insomnia just weeks before her wedding to fiancé Josh (Charles Michael Davis). One night, she has an unexpected encounter with Billy (Dave Annable), a bartender who is also having trouble sleeping. After discovering they can both drift off peacefully when lying next to each other, Lizzie suggests an unusual arrangement. She offers to help Billy fund his dream of opening a bar in exchange for keeping her company at night. However, their increasingly complicated arrangement starts to interfere with Lizzie’s wedding plans.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Netflix is kicking off its original holiday movie lineup with “A Dog’s Perfect Christmas,” a family drama based on W. Bruce Cameron’s 2019 novel. The story follows a family navigating a difficult festive season, with plenty of emotional moments alongside the usual Christmas cheer. Cameron co-wrote the screenplay with director Cathryn Michon, continuing their creative partnership after working together on “A Dog’s Purpose” and “A Dog’s Journey.” This is perfect for anyone who enjoys heartfelt animal movies and festive family stories.

Widowed grandfather Sander Goss (Dennis Quaid) is struggling to get along with his teenage granddaughter Ello (Brooke Lena Johnson) two years after losing his wife. When a sudden medical emergency leaves Ello’s mother in an induced coma just before Christmas, the family is thrown into turmoil. With the household struggling to cope, their loyal basset hound, Winstead (voiced by Thomas Haden Church), takes matters into his own paws. Alongside an energetic Corgi puppy named Ruby, Winstead sets out to bring the family together and help them prepare for Juliana’s return.

If you’d rather binge-watch a cozy mystery over the festive season, “Mistletoe Murders” is a great choice, especially with the series already climbing Netflix’s top 10. It originally began as an Audible audio drama in 2021, starring Cobie Smulders, before making the jump to television for Hallmark+ and the Hallmark Channel. The story brings a festive twist to the cozy mystery formula, pairing a charming small-town setting and plenty of Christmas decorations with a series of murder investigations. There’s nothing wrong with your holiday viewing having a little crime and suspense.

Emily Lane (Sarah Drew) runs Under the Mistletoe, a Christmas-themed gift shop in the small town of Fletcher’s Grove. Although she appears to be an ordinary shop owner, Emily has a mysterious past and a set of unusual skills that make her particularly good at investigating crimes. When a local murder puts one of her new friends under suspicion, Emily takes matters into her own hands to uncover the truth. Along the way, she crosses paths with Detective Sam Wilner (Peter Mooney), whose own investigations bring them closer together while raising questions about Emily’s real identity.

Another major Netflix original arriving this month is “Guarding Stars,” a festive romantic comedy based on Katherine Center’s bestselling novel “The Bodyguard.” The story follows a highly trained female protection agent who is assigned to look after a famous Hollywood actor, turning the usual action-romance formula on its head. Leighton Meester, best known for “Gossip Girl,” and Jared Padalecki of “Supernatural” and “Gilmore Girls” lead the cast, giving fans of both stars another reason to tune in. If you enjoy fun holiday romances with a little action and plenty of familiar faces, this one is worth adding to your watchlist.

Hannah Brooks (Leighton Meester) is a no-nonsense professional bodyguard assigned to protect Jack Stapleton (Jared Padalecki), a famous action movie star, during the Christmas holidays. When Jack returns to his family’s Montana ranch, Hannah accompanies him to keep him safe from an unwanted threat. To avoid raising suspicions about her real job, she agrees to pose as his girlfriend while staying with his family. However, as they spend more time together, their pretend relationship becomes increasingly complicated.

"A Dog's Perfect Christmas" (Netflix film)

From the bestselling author of A Dog’s Purpose, a tale of a family in crisis where a teenager, her grandfather, and his trusty basset hound struggle to keep the household together at Christmas.

A struggling pastor moves his family to a troubled New York neighborhood, where they must save a neglected church from foreclosure before Christmas.

#3326. This Hidden Device Could Free Up Gigawatts of Grid Power

The November issue of IEEE Spectrum is here!

Variable frequency drives can slash motors’ power use

Zurich-based ABB is one of several manufacturers of variable frequency drives (VFDs), such as this ACH580. VFDs could help make the millions of electric motors running in industrial facilities more energy efficient.

This article was originally published by Canary Media.

America’s energy supply crunch is driving a surge of federal and private investment in new electricity generation—from polluting gas turbines to cleaner developments like solar farms and geothermal plants. But gigawatts of power are already available for the taking across the U.S. economy in the form of wasted energy from an unexpected source: motors.

Some 50 million electric motors drive the fans, pumps, and compressors found in virtually every factory and building. Together, they gobble enough electricity to equal nearly a third of total U.S. power demand. Often, the motors use far more energy than they actually need to keep America’s machines humming.

Companies can install devices known as variable frequency drives, or VFDs, to make motors run super efficiently. Yet adoption remains relatively low, in part because of the perceived hassle of retrofitting equipment and because they’re typically not required. On average, only 16 percent of motor systems at industrial facilities and 4 percent of commercial-sector motors use VFDs, according to a 2021 market report by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

However, there are now more reasons than ever to equip the nation’s motors with power-saving devices, energy experts and device manufacturers say. They’re urging federal agencies, utilities, and deep-pocketed tech giants to spur a wider rollout of VFDs through financial incentives and efficiency standards.

For one, slashing motors’ power use would free up grid capacity for large electricity users like data centers and electric vehicles, they argue. It would help curb costs for factories that are switching from fossil-fueled heating systems to electrified, motor-based solutions like heat pumps—all at a time when industrial power prices are climbing fast. Plus, VFD technology has become far more sophisticated and less expensive to install than earlier iterations.

“This is low-hanging fruit that gives a lot [of energy] back and is reasonably simple,” Nik Sawe, a senior policy analyst at the nonpartisan think tank Energy Innovation, says of the technology.

Energy-wise, the main problem with electric motors is that they’re always running at full capacity. Consider an office building, which empties out in the evening. The heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning system can wind down in those hours, with dampers and valves restricting the flow of cold or hot air. But the motors and fans that drive the whole setup are still working in the background, wasting energy.

VFD technology, such as the Danfoss iC7 series, has gained some momentum in recent years among factories and buildings trying to combat rising electricity costs. Danfoss Drives

VFDs are electronic controllers with temperature sensors that continually adjust the speed of motors, automatically ramping up or down to match demand. The technology, which is also called adjustable speed drives, has the potential to curb a motor’s energy use by around 40 to 60 percent, says Neal Elliott, director emeritus of the American Council for an Energy-Efficient Economy.

All those energy reductions add up. Toyota, for example, installed VFDs on over 200 motors inside the HVAC system at its auto manufacturing plant in Georgetown, Kentucky, as part of a US $1.25 million pilot project in 2015. The automaker saved more than $700,000 in annual electricity costs thanks to the VFDs, and it continues to use the technology at other manufacturing facilities across the U.S., the company said by email.

“We’ve known for many, many years that there’s a huge opportunity for energy savings by varying the speed of the motor,” says Elliott, who noted that he literally wrote the book on energy-efficient motor systems in 2002.

Certain aspects of the technology have historically held the drives back since they debuted in the late 1960s. Measuring the flow of water, air, refrigerant—whatever is moving through the system that the motors are driving—was for decades an expensive engineering process. Accurately controlling motors to deliver the right amount of juice, at just the right time, faced similar issues.

But recent advances in sensors and machine-learning algorithms have significantly slashed the cost and complexity of using drives, Elliott says. Modern VFDs have also benefited from the increased production of advanced power chips that are used in high-voltage applications such as electric vehicles and solar power inverters.

Another long-standing challenge has been that commercial and industrial building developers often prioritize reducing upfront costs over netting long-term energy savings, and so they don’t always build to the highest efficiency levels, says Zack Valdez, senior director of regulatory and industry affairs at the National Electrical Manufacturers Association, whose members include drive and motor makers.

“If the facility that you’re putting it into doesn’t require it, then oftentimes people will overlook [VFDs], because they’re just trying to build to a minimum set of energy requirements,” he says. And if companies don’t install drives from the start, they’re likely less inclined to take time to retrofit an operating system.

The trade association recently launched a pilot program with manufacturers, utilities, and energy-efficiency groups to collect real-world data about how VFDs reduce motors’ electricity use and lower utility bills. The goal is to demonstrate how the technology can benefit not only individual facilities but also the wider grid—giving utilities a concrete reason to provide rebates for industrial customers.

Proponents say they hope the results will help the U.S. Department of Energy shape future efficiency measures and incentives that encourage adoption of the drives, including in federally owned buildings. Despite the Trump administration’s open hostility toward home appliance and equipment mandates, agency staff have apparently been receptive to discussing solutions that could meet the soaring power needs of data centers.

“If you added a drive to all the motors that are out there, you could provide [power for] up to five years of data center growth without having to build any new generation,” says Kirk Anderson, director of government relations and public affairs for ABB. The global manufacturing giant makes VFDs domestically near Milwaukee.

Anderson floated the idea of having tech companies help pay for factory owners to install VFDs to free up room on the grid. After all, hyperscalers are already spending many billions of dollars to revive shuttered nuclear plants, support next-generation geothermal projects, deploy fleets of grid-scale batteries, and supercharge the build-out of gas turbines and power plants.

“Instead of ‘bring your own power,’ it should be ‘offset your own power,’” he says, referring to a growing effort by states to get data centers to secure their own power resources and prevent rising costs for regular customers.

Michael Reckamp, the director of enterprise strategy for Danfoss Drives, North America, another VFD manufacturer, said that despite the traditionally low adoption rates, the technology has gained some momentum in recent years among factories and buildings as rising electricity costs and other grid-wide challenges make it harder to justify wasting energy.

Still, “it hasn’t permeated enough to get everyone utilizing it,” he says. “In the current situation, where we’re having so many issues with grids, brownouts, and now data centers wanting to take the load, I think there should be a renewed focus on putting drives out there to really reduce the stress on the grid and improve energy savings.”

Maria Gallucci is a clean-energy reporter with Canary Media.

#3325. Report: Apple and Samsung outperform rivals as smartphone chip shipments tumble 21%

According to Counterpoint Research, Apple and Samsung were the only major smartphone chip vendors to gain market share in Q3 2026, as global shipments declined 21% year-over-year. Here are the details.

At this point, most 9to5Mac readers are probably familiar with the challenges that smartphone vendors have been facing due to rising memory costs, and how Apple has managed to weather the impact better than many of its competitors.

Over the past few months, many reports have noted that while most smartphone vendors raised prices more than once throughout the year, Apple held off on increasing iPhone prices until September, with the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro series.

Those same reports have been showing the iPhone outperforming the broader market in smartphone, even as the industry experiences a sharp downturn.

That said, Counterpoint Research recently published a report (via MacMagazine) examining how rising memory costs and slowing smartphone demand have affected the global smartphone chip market.

According to the report, Apple remained in third place among smartphone chip vendors in the third quarter, with its market share increasing from 17% in Q3 2025 to 21%.

MediaTek still led the global smartphone SoC market with a 28% share (down 6 percentage points year-over-year), followed by Qualcomm with 22% (down from 25%).

After Apple, UNISOC ranked fourth with 13% (down from 14%), while Samsung remained in fifth with an 8% share, up from 6% in Q3 2025. Other manufacturers went from a 4% share to 8%.

Overall, the market saw a 21% decline year-over-year, though the report didn’t disclose how many chips were shipped during the quarter.

Commenting on the numbers, Counterpoint Research Senior Analyst Shivani Parashar said:

“We saw three notable flagship chipset launches in September 2026, based on TSMC’s 2nm process node: Apple’s A20 series, MediaTek’s Dimensity 9600 Pro and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series. These launches are expected to boost premium smartphone SoC shipments in Q4 2026, although volumes are still likely to remain below Q4 2025 levels.”

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects global smartphone chip shipments to decline 20% year-over-year in 2026, followed by another 3% to 4% drop in 2027. The research firm also expects memory prices to continue rising next year.

During its fiscal Q4 2026 earnings call, Apple described the current memory pricing situation as “unprecedented,” warning that further increases would continue to put pressure on its profit margins in the coming quarters.

If this sounds familiar, that’s because this is not Apple’s first attempt to help developers reduce cancellations.

Apple’s documentation notes that developers can create up to 10 retention messages per app, each associated with one or more subscriptions.

I had officially closed the book on volumizing hot brushes. Like half the internet, I fell victim to the Revlon One-Step craze a few years back. While it certainly had the smoothing factor down, it felt like it was actively ripping chunks of hair from my scalp with every pass.

My Dyson Airwrap attachment was undeniably gentler, sure, but it never quite delivered the rich, bouncy volume I was actually chasing. Eventually, I resigned myself to heatless curl rods to fake the blowout aesthetic — only to spend the rest of the day mourning the catastrophic amount of curl shrinkage.

Recently, I tested Wavytalk's Steam Sesh. After watching that flat iron tame my hair in 10 minutes flat, I haven’t shut up about steam tech to anyone within earshot. Naturally, my expectations for its sister tool, the Steamlift Pro, were high.

I’m relieved to report it didn’t just meet the bar, it completely cleared it.

The first sign of progress arrived before I even plugged it in. One minor gripe I had with the Steam Sesh was the trial-and-error setup, which practically forced you to scroll TikTok just to figure out how to seat the water tank properly.

Wavytalk clearly took notes. Right inside the box of the Steamlift Pro was a printed visual guide, removing any guesswork.

The mechanics will feel instantly familiar if you’ve used the straightener: pop out the removable tank, add water (distilled remains the smart play if you want to avoid mineral buildup), power it on, and turn to your target temperature. If you want that hit of hydration, hit the dedicated steam switch.

Down from $129 to $99, this 23% saving makes the Steamlift Pro a solid value. If you want bouncy, snag-free 90s volume with gentle steam tech instead of frying your curls on dry heat, grab it while it’s under $100.

Where hot air brushes usually fail curls is tension. Round blow-dry barrels rely on dense, stiff nylon bristles that grab too aggressively, catching on textured coils and snapping fragile strands mid-pull.

The Steamlift Pro swaps out that brutal bristle setup for an integrated 3D comb system built right into the body of the brush. Instead of violently tugging, the teeth firmly grip and separate each individual hair strand as the heated surface glides through.

For someone prone to breakage, the difference in hand-feel was immediate. There was zero scalp-tugging resistance, no terrifying crunch of snapping ends, and no tangled bird’s nest trapped around a rotating barrel. The steam continuously releases through the comb, softening coarse cuticle layers so the hair yields without brute physical force.

My routine was simple. I detangled thoroughly, split my hair into two manageable tiers (top and bottom), and worked in generous sections.

Rather than jumping straight into styling curls, I started by using the Steamlift Pro as a standard smoothing tool, gliding it straight down from roots to mid-lengths to stretch out my natural curl pattern.

Once the baseline was uniform, I went back through the ends to roll and bevel them under for that bouncy, layered finish.

The entire process took 15 minutes. My hair came out silky, glossy, and entirely frizz-free. Most importantly, I retained my actual length instead of watching several inches vanish.

Finding tools that respect coarse, curly, and fragile hair without requiring professional-level arm acrobatics is rare. At this stage in my hair routine, the Steamlift Pro is easily the most capable blowout styler I’ve tested. If you have thick, frizz-prone curls and have spent years burned by viral hot brushes, do not sleep on this steam lineup.

Smart city deployments have historically relied on cameras, sensors, and dashboards that capture data without delivering timely insight. Can the $179 Fitbit Edge beat the $249 Apple Watch SE 3?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I recently tested the fitness tracking performance of the Fitbit Edge vs. Apple Watch 12, and much to my surprise, the more affordable Fitbit came out on top against one of the best smartwatches in 2026.

But can the Fitbit Edge pull a repeat win against the Apple Watch SE 3? It is, after all, a more direct competitor to the Edge, both in terms of price and features, compared to the Series 12.

To find out, I walked exactly 5,005 steps (manually counted) with the Fitbit Edge logging my efforts from my left wrist and the Apple Watch SE 3 recording the workout from my right wrist. As a control for distance, climb, and pace, I also recorded the walk in the Strava app on my iPhone 16 Plus.

You can find the results of my Fitbit Edge versus Apple Watch SE 3 walk test below, along with the five biggest takeaways from the data, including an overall winner declared at the end.

But first, here's a quick rundown of the key differences between these two popular wearables. The Apple Watch SE 3 starts at $249, is iOS-only, and balances impressive health and fitness features with smart features galore.

The Fitbit Edge starts at $179, works with Android and iOS devices, and also boasts comprehensive holistic and workout-logging chops, but few smart features. That said, the more petite Fitbit Edge gets roughly a week of battery compared to about a day for the Apple Watch SE 3.

When it comes to logging a basic walking workout, both devices are evenly matched with onboard GPS and barometric altimeters for precise location and elevation tracking, along with continuous heart rate monitoring.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Fitbit Edge logged 5,016 steps during my roughly 45-minute walk, just eleven steps off from my actual total. The Apple Watch SE 3 didn't do too shabby either, logging 109 step fewer than my manual count.

As always, my rule of thumb for these tests is that any step count within roughly 100 steps of my actual total is considered excellent and well within a reasonable margin for error. While the SE 3 is just a hair outside this threshold, this is still a solid result for the entry-level Apple Watch.

One of the biggest differences between the Fitbit Edge and its predecessor, the Fitbit Charge 6, is that the newer model has an altimeter for logging climb data; the older model doesn't. More importantly, the Edge logs uphill efforts with proven accuracy, from my testing, and this demo only adds to that conclusion.

The Apple Watch SE 3, meanwhile, inflated my climb by a similar margin to the Apple Watch 12 in my previous walk test versus the Edge.

The Apple Watch SE 3 (worn on my right wrist) logged higher heart rate data than the Fitbit Edge; however, the Fitbit Edge calculated more calories burned during the walk.

Could this discrepancy in heart rate be a result of the devices tracking my workout from different wrists? Probably not. After all, the best Apple Watches and best fitness trackers, including the Edge, are designed to be worn on the wrist of your choice.

That said, it's up to you to set your chosen wrist preference in the settings/companion app, as I did for this test, to ensure the best possible data.

The Fitbit Edge has the Apple Watch SE 3 easily beat when it comes to overall battery performance; the former lasts up to a week per charge compared to 18-24 hours per charge for the latter.

However, when it comes to GPS battery life, the two are apparently quite evenly matched. Both devices burned through 6% battery during my ~45-minute walk, an outcome I wasn't expecting.

Ultimately, the Fitbit Edge outperformed the Apple Watch SE 3 in this 5,005-step comparison of fitness tracking performance.

The Edge calculated nearly the same amount of steps taken as the manual tally and nearly identical elevation gain data too. That said, the SE 3 was a tiny bit closer to the control distance-wise.

However, even with the Edge coming out on top, I'd still happily use either of these modern wearables as my go-to health and fitness tracker, which begs the question: which do you prefer, the Apple Watch SE 3 or the Fitbit Edge? Let me know in the poll below.

#3318. Livestream: Watch Labrinth create a song from scratch tonight using Apple’s new MacBook Pro

To promote the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, Apple is hosting a livestream in which singer-songwriter Labrinth will create a song from scratch overnight at the company’s Tower Theatre store in Downtown Los Angeles. Watch the livestream below.

Last week, Apple announced the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display at a special event in Los Angeles, where it invited members of the press and content creators to get an early look at the redesigned laptop.

Now, Apple is continuing its Los Angeles-centered promotional campaign with another event, this time involving singer-songwriter Labrinth.

Starting at 8 p.m. PT / 11 p.m. ET tonight, Labrinth will spend the night at Apple’s Tower Theatre store in Downtown LA, creating an entire song from scratch using the new MacBook Pro and Logic Pro.

The entire process will be livestreamed on his YouTube channel, allowing viewers to follow along in real time and ask questions as he works. Apple says the finished song will be released next week.

Tonight’s livestream comes ahead of the new MacBook Pro’s launch this Friday, November 6.

During last week’s demos, Apple showcased the laptop’s music production capabilities, including the ability to play virtual instruments directly on its touchscreen using Logic Pro.

Tune in below starting at 8 p.m. PT / 11 p.m. ET to watch Labrinth create his new song live from Apple’s Tower Theatre store.

#3317. Ralph Lauren (RL) Q2 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

Asia growth drove the beat, but Europe store traffic weighed on results.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Ralph Lauren Corporation (RL -7.35%) reported second-quarter results that exceeded management's internal projections, resulting in an upward revision of its full-year revenue and margin guidance. Management reported that performance was driven by double-digit growth in Asia and continued expansion in average unit retail across direct-to-consumer channels. The company added 1.7 million new customers in the quarter, focusing on women, luxury, and younger demographics through elevated marketing activations and sports sponsorships. Despite macroeconomic volatility in Europe impacting store traffic, management indicated that core product lines and high-potential categories like handbags and outerwear maintained strong momentum.

Corinna Van der Ghinst: With me today are Patrice Louvet, the company's President and Chief Executive Officer, and Justin Picicci, Chief Financial Officer. After prepared remarks, we will open up the call for your questions, which we ask that you limit to one per caller. During today's call, our financial performance will be discussed on a constant currency adjusted basis. Our reported results, including foreign currency, can be found in this morning's press release. We will also be making some forward-looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws, including our financial outlook. Forward-looking statements are not guarantees, and our actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied in the forward-looking statements. Our expectations contain many risks and uncertainties.

Principal risks and uncertainties that could cause our results to differ materially from our current expectations are detailed in our SEC filings. To find disclosures and reconciliations of non-GAAP measures that we use when discussing our financial results, you should refer to this morning's earnings release and to our SEC filings that can be found on our investor relations website. With that, I will turn the call over to Patrice.

Patrice Louvet: Thank you, Corinna. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining today's call. We delivered another strong quarter of progress on our Next Great Chapter: Drive plan. In a consumer landscape often shaped by ever-changing trends, the clarity of Ralph Lauren's values and purpose of inspiring the dream of a better life through authenticity and timeless style continues to set us apart. We stay true to who we are, and we have a proven ability to evolve with today's consumer. This is a powerful competitive advantage, and it is translating into sustained broad-based momentum and a resilient core consumer with significant opportunities ahead.

In the second quarter, our top and bottom line results exceeded our expectations, enabling us to take up our full year guidance once again. This performance reflects our momentum across markets, channels, and categories. Revenues increased 10%, led by double-digit growth in Asia. Our retail channels also grew low double digits, with similar comp growth across stores and digital, while wholesale increased at a solid mid-single-digit rate. Our ongoing investments behind our brand, products, and lifestyle experiences enabled us to stay on offense and continue our long-term elevation journey with further improvement in quality of sales and full price selling.

At the same time, we continued to invest in our long-term capabilities, such as talent and technology, while accelerating cash returns to shareholders through our durable dividend and repurchases. This balance of investment and shareholder returns reflects the power of the Ralph Lauren model. Our strong balance sheet, cash flows, and culture of operating discipline give us the flexibility to navigate a complex global backdrop while fueling future growth opportunities. Underpinning this model is a combination only Ralph Lauren can bring together: authentic lifestyle authority, cultural relevance, and timeless brand codes at global scale.

We are building on this distinctive advantage through the three strategic pillars of our plan, which, as a reminder, include, first, elevate and energize our lifestyle brand, second, drive the core and expand for more, and third, win in key cities with our consumer ecosystem. Starting with our efforts to elevate and energize our lifestyle brand. Through our rolling thunder of activations, we are engaging with consumers across the many facets of their lives, from the inspiration of the runway to the biggest stages in sports, entertainment, and more.

This enables us to deepen our connection with existing consumers around the world as we build lifetime value, while also inspiring a new generation with our cinematic storytelling and core values of optimism, quality, and authenticity. Key highlights from the quarter included, first, we continued to strengthen our position as one of the world's leading luxury lifestyle brands in sports, elevating traditionally local events into globally relevant, exciting brand moments. At Wimbledon, we combined the heritage and elegance of the tournament with Ralph Lauren's spectator style.

We activated across our top cities around the world, from our Sloane Square takeover in London to our Tokyo live viewing party and Douyin live shopping event in Hong Kong, and our Legends tennis exhibition match in New York Central Park with Andre Agassi, Caroline Wozniacki, Genie Bouchard, and James Blake. At the U.S. Open, we built on our longstanding partnership with an expanded 360-degree campaign, including our vintage-inspired collection, specialty pop-ups, and influencer activations. At the Goodwood Revival in the U.K., we brought our sophistication to the classic motorsports event for the fourth year, including a preview of our Polo Bar experience ahead of our London restaurant opening slated for 2028.

Together, these sports lifestyle campaigns allow us to showcase the breadth of the Ralph Lauren lifestyle while bringing consumers closer to the brand. They generated a combined 70 billion global impressions and more than $350 million in media value. Next, we immerse consumers in our vision of timeless style through our Spring 2027 Women's Collection Fashion Show in New York City, along with key celebrity dressing moments, including BTS at their Arirang World Tour at MetLife Stadium and at our Very Ralph documentary premiere in Seoul.

Beyond the quarter, we recently hosted our first-ever PoloFest in Tokyo, bringing Polo collectors, brand enthusiasts, and cultural voices together for a three-day experience as part of our year-long celebration of 50 years in Japan. These activations are driving strong, sustainable growth in new customer acquisition and retention. In the second quarter, we added 1.7 million new customers to our DTC businesses, led by Ralph Lauren stores. We continue to drive progress across brand equity metrics, including increased awareness, purchase intent, and net promoter score. We're also driving higher lifetime value and recruiting key consumer cohorts, led once again by women, luxury, and younger customers.

We increased our social media followers by mid-single digits to more than 72 million, led by Instagram, LINE, and Douyin, with a focus on our Summer of Sports and fashion show. This diversity of activations enables us to keep the brand fresh and relevant across each of our key markets, staying true to Ralph's vision while finding new ways to bring each generation into our world. This brand momentum is translating directly into increasing desirability and demand for our products. This takes me to our second key initiative, drive the core and expand for more. Ralph's vision has always been about a way of living.

This quarter, our talented creative teams brought that vision to life through our enduring icons, combined with seasonal newness across men's, women's, and children's. By reinforcing the core while expanding our lifestyle proposition, we are creating multiple avenues for durable growth and bringing our products to life through increasingly connected consumer ecosystems. Starting with our core, which represents more than 70% of our business, core product sales grew 10% in the second quarter. Recent highlights include our cotton cable and merino blend sweaters, linen poplin and oxford dyed shirts, icon chino caps, sport coats, and fleece. For the Fall 2026 season, our Litchfield and Red Rocks collections for men's Polo resonated particularly well with consumers.

In children's, we delivered a successful back-to-school with our collegiate-inspired Next Gen and New England-themed Middlebury collections, with strength across our sweaters, core mesh Polos, sweater dresses, and expanded outerwear proposition. Our high-potential categories, including women's apparel, outerwear, and handbags, grew low double digits for the quarter, ahead of total company growth. In women's, we drove excitement through our new micro cable collared cardigan and wool rugby sweaters, corduroy shirts, and Polo shirt dresses. Our strong outerwear performance was driven by our lightweight Bi-Swing and Bayport cotton windbreakers for men and icon windbreakers and barn jackets for women.

In handbags, we officially launched Polo Blaze, our most elevated foundational collection for Polo to date, marrying equestrian-inspired details with a downtown edge. Special releases this quarter included our U.S. Open collection, inspired by the heritage of tennis and the spirit of New York, delivering our strongest sell-throughs around the event to date, and our collaborations with Gee's Bend and second capsule drop with TÓPA, both part of our groundbreaking Artist in Residence series, focused on empowering and celebrating artisans within the communities that have historically inspired our designs.

As we turn to holiday, we will continue to invite consumers to step into the cinematic worlds that Ralph created, with timeless, high-quality products, a compelling value proposition, and styling that only we can deliver. Turning to our third key initiative, win in key cities with our consumer ecosystem. We are creating unique lifestyle experiences to immerse consumers in the world of Ralph Lauren, bringing together product, hospitality, and storytelling in our top 30 cities around the world, while also laying the groundwork for long-term growth in our next 20 cities. Within DTC, which comprises the majority of our business, global comps increased 10%, led once again by our Ralph Lauren stores and digital commerce.

By region, Asia increased 28%, driven by 24% comps and growth across all key markets. China sales remained strong, increasing more than 35%, while Japan and Korea were also up double digits as we continue to invest behind localized brand activations and experiences. Europe delivered low single-digit growth this quarter, in line with our plan, despite industry traffic headwinds and on top of last year's strong compares. We drove another quarter of strong results ahead of expectations in our largest region, North America, with healthy demand in both our retail and wholesale channels. With regards to our store base, we opened 22 new owned and partner stores globally this quarter as we deepened our presence in our top cities.

Highlights included Seaport in Boston, including our first Ralph's Coffee location in Massachusetts, new men's and women's standalone stores in London, Sloane Square, Saint-Tropez, France, Beijing Hopson One, and Galaxy Promenade in Macau. On the digital front, we expanded our RL mobile app to Japan following our successful launch in Korea earlier this year, with early sales performance and downloads exceeding our expectations. We also grew our connected retail and clienteling capabilities across several markets in Asia this quarter, enabling our teams to serve consumers with greater personalization and consistency. Finally, touching on our enablers. Our business continues to be supported by our five key enablers.

Recent highlights include, first, as part of our focus on advanced technology, AI, and analytics, we are investing in new capabilities that help our teams move faster, create more personalized consumer experiences, and operate with greater precision. In addition to expanding our mobile app and clienteling in Asia this quarter, we continued our journey to enhance visibility on key LLMs. We also launched a test on WhatsApp Concierge, a digital assistant that allows customers to interact directly with our brand on the WhatsApp platform. Following our initial test with OpenAI earlier this year, we are further scaling advertising on the platform for holiday gifting and cultural moments. In addition, we are advancing our commitment to the communities we serve.

We recently announced a new partnership with the Korea National Cancer Center Foundation to establish a new Ralph Lauren Cancer Center in Goyang, our first in Asia and fifth globally, part of our broader long-standing commitment to more equitable access to cancer care. We were proud to be recently named one of the world's best employers by Forbes, reflecting the power of the people and culture that make Ralph Lauren so special. In closing, Ralph and I are encouraged by our team's progress in this second year of our Next Great Chapter: Drive plan in the midst of an ever-evolving global operating landscape.

As we head into the important holiday season, our consumer remains at the center of everything we do. With that in mind, we will continue to lean into our long-term elevation journey, investing in our strategic priorities to deliver sustainable growth and value creation into the future, including developing innovative campaigns that build desirability and engagement and grow lifetime value, creating timeless, high-quality products that offer compelling value and earn consumers' trust, and winning in our top cities through unique brand experiences that immerse consumers in the world of Ralph Lauren.

These diversified engines of growth and our increasingly elevated consumer base, all underpinned by our iconic brand, continue to drive resilience in our business model and consistency in our performance. With that, I'll hand it over to Justin, and I'll join him at the end to answer your questions.

Justin Picicci: Thanks, Patrice, and good morning, everyone. Our second quarter performance underscores our growing brand desirability around the world, with results exceeding our expectations across both revenue and profitability. This reflects broad-based consumer demand and the strength of our diversified growth model against a dynamic operating backdrop. Revenues increased 10%, ahead of our mid-single-digit outlook for the quarter, with growth across every region. Our brand and products continue to resonate with consumers globally, and full-price momentum supported gross and operating margin expansion above expectations. Notably, we delivered this performance while continuing to invest in the strategic initiatives that will fuel sustainable long-term growth and value creation.

This combination of second quarter outperformance and sustained brand momentum gives us confidence to raise our full-year outlook once again. First, let me walk you through our financial highlights from the second quarter, which, as a reminder, are provided on a constant currency adjusted basis. Total company second quarter revenue grew 10%, driven by better-than-expected performance in both our direct-to-consumer and wholesale channels. By region, Asia led our performance, increasing 28%, followed by North America, up 6%, and Europe, up 3%. Total company retail comps also increased 10%, with growth across both our own digital and brick-and-mortar channels. Total company adjusted gross margin expanded 220 basis points to 70.2%, ahead of our outlook.

The increase was driven by AUR growth, favorable geographic mix, and lower product costs, which more than offset modest pressure from higher labor and non-cotton material costs in the quarter. AUR increased 9%, ahead of our plan, and on top of 12% growth last year. The increase was broad-based and reflected balanced contributions from product elevation, favorable channel and geographic mix, and selective pricing actions and lower promotional activity. For the third quarter, we are currently planning for mid-single-digit AUR growth on top of last holiday's exceptionally strong 18% increase. Our outlook continues to be supported by our ongoing brand elevation strategy, with the flexibility to further reduce discounting based on consumer demand and selling trends.

Adjusted operating expenses increased 11%, or 70 basis points as a percentage of sales compared to last year, as higher marketing more than offset leverage in non-marketing expenses. Marketing increased to 8.6% of sales, up from 7.8% last year, reflecting increased investments to amplify key campaigns, including our New York fashion show and sponsorships of Wimbledon and the U.S. Open. Our multi-year progress in sustained new customer acquisition, healthy consumer metrics, and attractive returns reinforces our confidence to continue expanding our marketing programs across our top cities. We now expect marketing investment to represent approximately 8%-8.5% of sales in fiscal 2027, compared to approximately 8% previously.

Even with this higher investment, second quarter adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 15.5%, ahead of our plan, while operating income grew 21%. This underscores our ability to expand profitability while continuing to make investments in our brand and capabilities that support durable growth. Turning to segment performance, and starting with North America, second quarter revenue grew 6% at the high end of our expectations. In North America retail, second quarter comps increased 6% on top of a double-digit compare last year, with balanced growth across our digital and brick-and-mortar channels. Digital comps increased 5%, supported by solid traffic, full-funnel marketing activations, and continued merchandising optimization.

North America wholesale revenue grew 8%, driven by healthy replenishment and seasonal orders. Results included approximately four points of benefit from planned timing shifts from the second half of the year. We continue to expect North America wholesale performance to moderate in the second half as we lap these timing benefits and accelerate our strategic reduction of off-price sales and lower-tier full-price stores. Our underlying growth in the channel remains healthy, with strong full-price sellout trends and continued market share gains. Turning to Europe, second quarter revenue increased 3%, modestly ahead of our expectations. Europe wholesale increased 4% on top of double-digit growth last year.

Underlying sellout trends remain in line with our full-year outlook, and we continue to proactively manage our sell-in to align with consumer demand and maintain healthy inventories in the channel. Europe retail comps declined 1% as we lapped an exceptionally strong 10% compare last year amid a challenging macro environment. While the region continues to face pressure from weaker store traffic across several of our key markets, we are taking targeted strategic actions to drive stronger consumer engagement, increased conversion, and higher basket sizes in our stores.

Looking ahead to the second half of the year, we continue to invest behind our strongest brand and consumer opportunities in the region, including marketing activations and targeted consumer engagement, building on our growing brand desirability to support both near and long-term growth. Moving to Asia, second quarter revenue increased 28%, reflecting broad-based growth across all key markets. Retail comps grew 24%, with double-digit growth across every channel. Our Asia digital ecosystem also delivered double-digit growth, with strong contributions from our own digital commerce sites. By market, China continued to lead our performance, with sales up more than 35% in the quarter, driven by healthy comps and high-quality new customer recruitment.

Japan and Korea also delivered strong double-digit growth, supported by localized brand activations and sustained consumer engagement. Our full-funnel marketing activations throughout the region are building deeper connections with consumers, and we continue to see substantial opportunity to build awareness, deepen engagement, and expand our presence across key markets where our luxury lifestyle positioning continues to resonate. Moving to the balance sheet. Our fortress balance sheet and strong cash flow generation continue to provide meaningful strategic flexibility, enabling us to invest through periods of volatility, pursue compelling growth opportunities, and return capital to our shareholders, all while maintaining prudent financial discipline.

During the second quarter, we repurchased approximately $250 million in shares, bringing our year-to-date repurchases to $500 million and completing our buyback plans for fiscal 2027. We remain on track to return over $2 billion to shareholders, including through dividends and repurchases over our three-year drive plan. We ended the period with $1.8 billion in cash and short-term investments and $1.2 billion in total debt. We continue to manage inventories closely against demand in each of our regions. Second quarter net inventory decreased 8% in constant currency, reflecting last year's elevated tariff-related inventory base. Excluding the impact of tariffs, net inventory declined approximately 2%.

As we enter the holiday season, our inventories remain healthy, current, and well-positioned to support demand across geographies and channels while preserving flexibility. Looking ahead, our outlook for fiscal 2027 remains based on our best current assessment of the operating environment, including the geopolitical backdrop, foreign currency dynamics, and broader macroeconomic conditions. For fiscal 2027, we now expect constant currency revenue growth of mid to high single digits on a 52-week comparable basis, centered around 6%-7%, up from our prior outlook of 5%-6%. This increase largely reflects our better-than-expected second quarter results, along with a modestly stronger outlook for the second half, supported by our continued brand momentum.

As previously discussed, we continue to expect first-half growth to be stronger than second-half growth, reflecting the timing of this year's marketing activations and other investments, the timing of planned wholesale shipment shifts and strategic off-price reductions, and more challenging year-over-year comparisons in certain of our key markets. Importantly, our outlook continues to assume healthy underlying growth in the second half, in line with our long-term plan. Foreign currency is now expected to negatively impact revenue growth by approximately 40-60 basis points this year, based on current exchange rates. As a reminder, fiscal 2027 includes a 53rd week, which is expected to add approximately one point to revenue growth and slightly benefit operating margin.

By region for fiscal 2027, we now expect North America revenue to grow approximately low to mid-single digits, up from low single digits previously. We are encouraged by our strong first-half performance in the region and the continued momentum across our DTC and full-price wholesale channels. We still expect this solid underlying growth to be partly offset by accelerated strategic actions to improve quality of sales and exit lower-tier doors, notably in the back half of the year, as we further elevate and strengthen our long-term position in the marketplace. We now expect Europe revenue to grow approximately low single digits, compared to low to mid-single digits previously.

This outlook reflects positive underlying growth, partly offset by increased pressure on consumer traffic and broader macroeconomic volatility in the second half of the year. We remain focused on driving high-quality near-term results while continuing to invest behind long-term brand elevation and margin expansion. We now expect Asia revenue to increase low teens, up from our prior outlook of high single to low double digits, driven by our stronger-than-expected first-half results, along with ongoing brand momentum across our key markets in the region. We now expect full-year operating margin to expand approximately 80-100 basis points in constant currency, up from our prior guidance of 60-80 basis points, largely driven by our better-than-expected second quarter results.

We are also raising our full-year gross margin outlook to approximately 80-100 basis points of expansion, compared to our prior guidance of 50-70 basis points. This reflects our stronger-than-expected Q2 results, along with our updated view on U.S. tariffs, which assumes the prevailing rate of approximately 10% through December, followed by a return to reciprocal rates in the high teens in our fiscal fourth quarter. We continue to expect both gross and operating margin expansion to be weighted towards the first half of the fiscal year, reflecting normalizing AUR growth and the timing of key marketing activations, as well as our previously disclosed timing shifts in wholesale shipments.

Our guidance continues to exclude the benefit of tariff refunds, which are not included in our adjusted non-GAAP results. As part of our long-term capital allocation strategy, related proceeds received will be primarily reinvested in the business, as well as directed toward initiatives that strengthen and advance our purpose and values. Foreign currency is now expected to benefit gross margin by approximately 10-30 basis points and have a roughly neutral impact on operating margin in fiscal 2027. For the third quarter, we expect constant currency revenue to increase approximately low to mid-single digits, centered around 3%-4%.

This outlook includes approximately one point of negative impact from planned wholesale timing shifts and strategic off-price reductions in the quarter, with underlying growth of roughly mid-single digits. Foreign currency is expected to negatively impact revenues by approximately 50-100 basis points. We expect operating margin to expand approximately 50-70 basis points in constant currency, with gross margin expansion more than offsetting higher marketing investments in the holiday period. Foreign currency is expected to benefit gross margin by about 20-40 basis points and have a roughly neutral to 20 basis point benefit to operating margin in the quarter.

We expect our third quarter tax rate to be in the range of 23%-24%, while the full year tax rate is still expected to be in the range of 21%-22%. In closing, our teams continue to deliver against both our near-term commitments and long-term strategic priorities. This quarter's results demonstrate the strength of our diversified growth model, the benefits of our elevation strategy, and the discipline with which we are investing for the future, underscoring the enduring relevance of Ralph's timeless vision around the world. While the external environment remains dynamic, we are focused on what we can control, continuing to drive brand and product desirability, enhancing quality of sales, operating with discipline, and investing behind high-return growth opportunities.

Together, these actions position us well to deliver on our fiscal 2027 commitments while strengthening the foundation for durable long-term value creation for all of our stakeholders. With that, let's open up the call for your questions.

My favorite tips and features for the iPhone Duo

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Apple’s biggest ever change to the iPhone formula brought some unique features and scene-stealing upgrades when it was revealed back in September. But now that we’re actually getting our hands on the device (well, some of us are), it turns out there’s a lot more underneath that 7.6-inch nano texture display to discover.

Alongside the likes of Smart Take and Kid Cue, the iPhone Duo has a bunch of cool tricks that can help with usability or productivity that I’ve started to use during my time with the phone. If you’re planning to pick up an iPhone Duo for yourself, you may want to give some of these a try.

The iPhone Duo is the first iPhone to allow you to run two apps side-by-side but only if you’re holding it in landscape orientation. One of the frustrations our Global Editor-in-Chief Mark pointed out recently is that you lose the functionality as soon as you rotate it into portrait mode.

This isn’t exactly a silver bullet to that problem, but you can utilize picture-in-picture to snap a video to the top of the portrait orientation whilst keeping a separate app running below, or vice versa.

To accomplish it, start any video app and minimize it into picture-in-picture mode. When you start a second app, the minimized video will generate a new button next to the full-screen option that automatically expands it to just the top of the display. It will automatically resize the secondary app to take up the lower half of the screen.

Over the years, iPhone users have grown accustomed to swiping down from the top-right of the display to open the Control Center. On the Duo, you’re given a one-handed shortcut through the new icon that displays your Wi-Fi and cell reception.

Usually, it just sits there being useful, but if you tap on it, it’ll launch you straight into the Control Center without having to reach up with your thumb to swipe down.

Sign up to the Tom's iGuide weekly newsletter with coverage on everything from product launches to software updates, this is your go-to source for the latest updates on all the best Apple content.

Apple has borrowed the Edge Light feature from macOS and added it to the iPhone Duo’s repertoire. If you’ve not used it before (I hadn’t) then it turns the border of your display into a virtual ring light. This serves to give you some nice illumination when you’re on a video call in dim light.

Edge Light is only available when the iPhone Duo is unfolded. To enable it, open Control Center while on a video call and tap the colored control bar labelled “FaceTime controls”. Then tap on the light bulb button next to "Edge Light" in the video effects menu. You can manually adjust the brightness and hue of the light or hit the Automatic toggle to have the Duo analyze the ambient light in the room and adjust accordingly.

The decision to put the iPhone Duo’s volume controls on the top of the phone is one that takes some getting used to. If you’re using the phone unfolded, and you happen to rotate it with the volume keys on the bottom, things can get awkward. That’s because the default configuration fixes the right button as volume up and the left as volume down — even if you’re holding the phone upside down.

If you want to set the buttons to dynamically adjust depending on the Duo’s orientation, you can find that option under Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Fixed Position Volume.

Once you disengage it, the button on the right in any position will always increase the volume while the left decreases it. It would still be better to have them on the side in the first place, but that’s a job for the iPhone Duo 2.

Tucked inside the Shortcuts app is a new feature that’s exclusive to the iPhone Duo called “Open or Closed.” This lets you automate a shortcut based on whether the phone is open or closed. So, for example, you could create one to open the Books app automatically when you unfold the iPhone Duo.

In order to activate it, you need to open the Shortcuts app on your iPhone Duo, tap the + button in the bottom corner, then tap Edit in the top right corner. From there, tap the Automation option that appears at the top of the options list and scroll down to “Open or Closed” under the Display section.

Once you have that in place, find the Open App command and choose the app you want to launch. When you exit the Shortcuts app it will activate immediately.

Apple missed iOS 27.1 for all non-folding iPhones, instead jumping straight to iOS 27.2 (and now, iOS 27.3) for the likes of the iPhone 18 Pro Max and leaving iOS 27.1 a Duo exclusive. In all likelihood, that was due to some of the custom designs and features only available on the Duo.

As the Duo gets into more hands around the world and developers start to optimize their apps for the first folding iPhone, I expect we’ll see many more cool new Duo exclusive features coming to the fore. I’m particularly interested to see if Apple can expand on Split View multitasking to make it even better as the Duo matures.

Galaxy S27 Ultra leaks are coming in fast

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra is coming, and it could be arriving sooner than you think. The big phone launches of 2026 are effectively over, now that the new iPhones are out of the way, and that means we can start looking at what major releases 2027 will have to offer.

Samsung is usually the first out of the gate, and rumor has it that the launch will be a little earlier than we're used to — suggesting a January release window. The Unpacked event is also said to include four new Galaxy S27-series phones, with a Pro model set to join the usual lineup. But, as ever, the Galaxy S27 Ultra is set to be the star of the show, with all the latest and best hardware Samsung has to offer.

Here's everything we know about the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra so far.

200MP main, 50MP ultrawide, 50MP telephoto with 4x or 5x optical zookm

163.76 x 78.25 x 7.97mm (6.44 x 3.0 x 0.31 inches)

We're not expecting any major changes to the size of the Galaxy S27 Ultra, and recently-leaked dummy units suggest that the dimensions of the upcoming phone will be very similar to those of the Galaxy S26 Ultra. And by very similar, I mean practically identical, with only a fraction of a millimeter's difference in width and thickness.

However, the big changes are set to happen on the back of the phone. Samsung is widely expected to ditch the vertical camera array of past Galaxy phones, in favor of a full-width camera bar — similar to that of the iPhone 18 Pro. This change is also supposed to come with the loss of the secondary telephoto lens, and turn the Ultra model into a triple-lens camera for the first time.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Recently-leaked dummy units also suggest that the Ultra will retain its built-in S Pen, and rumor has it that Qi2 magnets will finally be added to the phone itself. That means no more having to buy special magnetic cases to make the most out of using Qi2 chargers and accessories. However, this feature may be exclusive to the Ultra and Pro models, with the Standard and Plus options missing out.

The one thing that isn't a mystery is the S27 Ultra's performance hardware. We assumed the phone would come with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, and a recent leak seemingly confirmed that. Not that it was ever doubted that Samsung would opt for the most powerful Qualcomm chip on the market. The only real question we have is whether the phone will have a standard Extreme chip, or if a custom "for Galaxy" variant will be developed to offer stronger performance.

Our own early tests of the Extreme, using Qualcomm's reference device, reveal that the chip performed 29% better in Geekbench 7's single-core benchmark, and 16.3% better in the multi-core test. 3DMark's Solar Bay Extreme test shows a 49% increase in graphical power, or a 40% increase in Wildlife Extreme. Meanwhile AnTuTu's General AI benchmark showed an 18.4% increase, or a crazy 118% increase in AnTuTu's LLM AI test.

Obviously things are going to be a little different in a commercial phone, rather than a reference device that's built to perform well. But it shows just how much of an improvement we should see when the Galaxy S27 Ultra arrives next year. Needless to say this is going to be a powerful phone with a lot of AI capabilities.

Very little is known about the Galaxy S27 Ultra's cameras right now, other than the fact Samsung is seemingly scrapping the secondary telephoto lens. This means the Ultra model will match other premium phones with a single zooming lens, which we assume will still be the same 50MP lens with 5x optical magnification we saw on the Galaxy S26 Ultra.

While that news may be disappointing to some, it's not a huge loss. The second telephoto lens was always fairly underpowered, with the last iteration offering 10MP of resolution and 3x optical zoom. The quality wasn't bad, but it also wasn't really a necessary feature to have. Particularly since telephoto lenses are expensive, hence why they're mostly found on premium phones, and take up a lot of space. Removing the second one adds extra space to the S27 Ultra, and hopefully helps avoid another price hike.

This would be the perfect time for Samsung to add variable optical zoom, which has been rumored for a few years and effectively squeezes two telephoto lenses into one. Sadly it's unclear whether that will actually happen, and the same is true for the possibility of getting variable aperture — a feature Samsung last offered in 2019.

Rumors instead suggest that the telephoto may drop to 4x magnification, with a larger 1/1.9-inch sensor to compensate. However, there are conflicting reports, and the S27 Ultra may instead just get the exact same zooming lens as the S26 Ultra.

We know software is going to be a huge part of the Samsung Galaxy S27 series, as it has been for the last few generations of Galaxy phones. Galaxy AI is one of those things that isn't going to vanish overnight, though at this early stage we have absolutely no idea what sort of features and capabilities will be coming to the S27 Ultra and its cohorts.

One possibility is the addition of MyFanCam, an AI-powered feature that debuted on the Galaxy Z Fold 8. It works with existing footage that you've filmed, and uses AI to focus on a person of your choice. There's no reason why it couldn't exist on a Galaxy S phone, and the S27 launch is the perfect place to do it — especially if it has some much-needed upgrades, like the ability to focus on animals as well. We should also expect the phones to run on OneUI 9, possibly the updated OneUI 9.5, which is based on Android 17.

But, for the time being, any additional software and AI upgrades on the S27 Ultra are a complete mystery.

The release of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 saw Samsung finally embrace silicon carbon batteries. The main benefit is that the increased energy density means you can include more battery capacity without increasing the actual physical dimensions of the battery. This allows for larger batteries that aren't physically larger, and don't increase the size and weight of phones by any significant amount.

Leaks suggest that Samsung will be adopting the same technology in the Galaxy S27 Ultra, increasing the size of the battery from 5,000 mAh to 5,700 mAh. That's quite an upgrade, considering Galaxy Ultra phones have been stuck at 5,000 mAh for the past six years, though whether it will help the S27 Ultra climb the ranks of our best phone battery life page isn't clear yet. We'll need to wait and see how it performs during battery life testing.

Furthermore, it's unclear whether charging speed will change at all, considering the S26 Ultra upped the ante from 45W wired charging to 60W. However the rumored inclusion of Qi2 magnetic charging means that wireless charging should be much easier — even if it doesn't happen any faster.

There's still a lot we don't know about the Galaxy S27 Ultra, but so far we're hearing about some promising things. Sure, the loss of a camera lens might be disappointing to some, but we are still getting some positive changes. A larger battery is something Galaxy users have been demanding for years, and the inclusion of Qi2 magnets means that Samsung is now on par with Apple and Google in the wireless charging game.

There is still plenty of time for new information to leak, and that means we'll start getting a more complete picture of what the Galaxy S27 Ultra has to offer as the weeks and months roll on. Until the inevitable January Unpacked, where Samsung reveals the whole lineup in full. But until then, be sure to check back here for all the latest news and rumors about the upcoming flagships.

#3314. Insurer Guardian hands 1 million dental calls a year to Sierra’s AI agents

The US insurer will also use Bret Taylor's startup for payments and claim status questions.

Guardian Life signed a multi-year deal with Sierra to use its AI agents for about 1 million dental benefit verification calls a year, plus payments and claim status checks. It is Guardian’s third AI partnership in a year, after HCLTech and Avantos.

US insurer Guardian Life is handing some of its busiest customer service work to AI agents from Sierra, the startup run by former Salesforce co-chief executive Bret Taylor. The two signed a multi-year partnership, Guardian said on Thursday.

Guardian will use Sierra for about 1 million calls a year to check dental benefits, plus payments and questions about claim status. It says the aim is faster answers, but it has not shared any targets or financial terms. Sierra has argued that AI agents should be paid per result, not per seat.

“No one should have to sit on hold to check on a claim or confirm dental benefits,” said Taylor, Sierra’s chief executive and co-founder.

Michael Prestileo, Guardian’s chief strategy officer, said the deal would let staff focus on the cases where “human judgment and connection matter most.”

It is Guardian’s third AI deal in a year. In July, it signed a seven-year deal with HCLTech, which is taking over Guardian’s India centre and nearly 2,000 of its staff. In February, it invested in Avantos, an AI platform for financial advisers.

Sierra, launched in February 2024, says it works with 46% of the Fortune 50. It raised $950M at a $15B valuation in May. Rivals are consolidating: Salesforce, which Taylor once co-ran, is buying Fin for $3.6B.

It has been adding features fast. Last month, it teamed up with Stripe so its agents can take card payments during calls, and with Meta on an open standard for personal AI agents.

#3313. Resident Evil director Zach Cregger explains why the iPhone is vital to his work

There have been a number of high-profile movies technically shot on iPhone, but in most cases they are using the same professional cinematography kit they would use with other cameras, including lenses costing tens of thousands of dollars.

Resident Evil director Zach Cregger uses his own iPhone in a rather different way, taking an approach that could be useful to amateur and professional filmmakers alike …

There’s an ongoing debate about how meaningful it is to claim that a high-profile movie, ad, or keynote video was shot on iPhone. Naysayers argue that the quality is all down to the professional lenses, lighting rigs, and editing employed, while those on the other side of the fence point out that everything was captured by the iPhone sensor.

Cregger mostly sidesteps all of that, describing his own use of an iPhone for shot planning, creating photo boards that accurately represent the image that will be captured by each of the Pro lenses he intends to use.

We grew up with video games informing our visual sense just as much as movies and television did, and I feel like I’m able to make a movie that involves the gameplay. [Here] I have a wide angle lens, our protagonist is in the center of the frame as he’s moving, we’re following locked right behind him when he looks right and we swing, right. His attention is dictating where the camera goes, and I think that the effect of that is is a much more immersive horror experience where you’re feeling informed.

I’m a hyper prepper. I’ve got the iPhone that is, like, always on me. I’ll go to the location with my cinematographer and I’ll use Cadrage, an app that approximates different lenses, and I will basically plan out the sequence. I will know exactly what shot is going to cut to what shot, and I will print out these images and everyone will know we’re using this lens for these shots. This is what’s going to be in the frame, and there’s no guesswork.

He does, however, add that an iPhone is all that you need to make a movie, even if his own budgets give him access to rather more expensive kit.

Anybody can make a movie with what’s in your pocket right now.

At the other end of the scale, I use my iPhone in a similar way to him when planning my own amateur videos. I take still photos to create a photo board so that I have a visual reference for each of my planned shots. The videos themselves may be shot on my Blackmagic rig, my iPhone, or some mix of the two.

You can watch Cregger talk through his process for Apple TV here.

This will continue to be a priority for Alan and his team, as they look to help ensure Texas, has the infrastructure required to maintain reliability and support future economic growth. that is why when we release Q4 results in February, we plan to announce a 2027 through 2031 base capital plan that is expected to reflect, among other things, a significant increase of approximately 20% over Oncor's existing $47.5 billion capital plan.
