#3252. Crane NXT (CXT) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Acquisitions drove sales higher, but organic growth and margins told a more mixed story this quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Crane NXT, Co. (CXT -3.78%) reported third-quarter results characterized by revenue growth driven by acquisitions and organic strength in the security segment, offset by softening demand in specific industrial hardware markets. Management reported multiple long-term contract renewals, including a 10-year agreement with the U.S. government for micro-optics and currency paper. The company raised its full-year earnings per share guidance midpoint while lowering its total sales growth outlook to approximately 14% to account for project delays in life sciences and retail hardware. Capital allocation remains focused on debt reduction and organic investments, specifically in micro-optics capacity expansion in the U.S. and Malta.

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Crane NXT Q3 2026 earnings call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speaker's presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, you will need to press star 11 on your telephone. You will then hear an automated message advising your hand is raised. To withdraw your question, please press star 11 again. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker today, John Walsh, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Walsh: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to the Crane NXT third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that the presentation slides we will reference today are available in the Investor Relations section of our website at cranenxt.com. A replay of today's call will also be available on our website following the conclusion of our remarks. Before we begin, please review the forward-looking statements disclaimer and non-GAAP disclosures on slide two. Our comments today are subject to the risks, uncertainties, and other important factors described in our earnings release, Form 10-K, and subsequent SEC filings.

Reconciliations of the non-GAAP measures discussed today to their most directly comparable GAAP measures are available in the earnings release and presentation on our Investor Relations website. Joining me today are Aaron Saak, President and Chief Executive Officer, and Christina Cristiano, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. We will review our third quarter highlights, financial and operational performance, and updated 2026 outlook before taking your questions. After our prepared remarks, we will open the call for questions. With that, I'll turn the call over to Aaron.

Aaron Saak: Thank you, John, and good morning. I want to begin by thanking our Crane NXT associates around the world for their continued focus on our customers and strong execution during the quarter. The key takeaway from the third quarter is that we continue to execute against our value creation priorities. We strengthened future revenue visibility through long-term commercial wins, delivered another quarter of strong operational performance, generated robust free cash flow, continued to advance the Antares Vision integration, and we're raising our full-year adjusted EPS guidance midpoint. Slide three highlights the progress we made during the quarter. First, we secured multiple long-term awards across the portfolio.

At Crane Currency, we signed multi-year renewals with the U.S. government for micro-optics and currency paper, and this adds to the U.S. passport paper win from the second quarter. The Bank of Canada also announced that its new $20 banknote will feature our micro-optics security technology, an important new customer win that expands our position with a leading global central bank. Within Crane Authentication, we renewed a multi-year agreement to provide enhanced security features for a global transaction card customer. In DTT, a large multinational food brand selected Antares Vision for a turnkey traceability and serialization solution, reflecting the team's domain expertise and track record on complex, large-scale deployments.

We also continue to expand CPI's multi-vendor service offerings into kiosks, smart safes, and self-checkout systems. Together, these awards strengthen our visibility into revenue growth for 2027 and beyond. We also delivered another quarter of strong operational performance, led by organic sales growth of 7% and 60 basis points of adjusted margin expansion in SAT, driven by volume leverage, execution of productivity initiatives, and acquisition synergies within Crane Authentication. In DTT, the Antares Vision integration continues to progress as expected. We are deploying the Crane Business System and have completed multiple Kaizen events focused on productivity and growth. These actions are reducing lead times, optimizing our footprint, and creating cross-selling opportunities across the portfolio.

Additionally, we continue to invest in innovation at Antares Vision, including new AI-enabled inspection technologies that combine advanced vision systems with our broader serialization and traceability capabilities, as highlighted at the recent PACK EXPO in Chicago. During the quarter, we also generated strong free cash flow, giving us confidence in achieving our year-end net leverage target of approximately 2.3 times. Based on our performance in Q3 and the visibility we have to the rest of the year, we are raising the midpoint of our full-year adjusted EPS guidance while narrowing the range, as our focus on execution and operational productivity will offset anticipated market softness in DTT markets.

I would now like to turn the call over to Christina to review our financial performance in more detail.

Christina Cristiano: Thank you, Aaron, and good morning, everyone. I also want to thank our associates around the world for their hard work and strong execution in the third quarter. Turning to slide four, third-quarter sales were $497 million, up 12% year over year. Organic sales increased 1%, driven by continued strength in SAT. Adjusted EBITDA increased 4% to $127 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.6%, down 190 basis points year over year, reflecting the expected dilution from the recent Antares Vision acquisition. We continue to expect full-year total company adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 24%. Adjusted EPS was $1.28, which was flat year over year, as higher adjusted operating profit was offset by higher interest expense from the acquisition.

Adjusted free cash flow was $98 million, up 15% year over year, with very strong free cash flow conversion of approximately 132%. We remain on track to achieve our full-year conversion guidance of approximately 90%-110%. Turning to SAT on slide five, third-quarter sales were $244 million, up approximately 6% year-over-year. Organic sales increased 7%, with similar growth in Crane Currency and Crane Authentication. Adjusted EBITDA increased 9% to $71 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 60 basis points to 29.2%. This increase was driven by Crane Authentication synergies, volume leverage, and favorable mix. SAT backlog increased 8% to approximately $482 million and remains at near record high levels.

We are booking orders into the second half of 2028 with meaningful visibility into continued customer demand. To meet growing international demand, we are accelerating initiatives to increase capacity, including investing in additional micro-optics production lines in the U.S. and Malta, as previously discussed. Turning to DTT on slide six, third-quarter sales were $254 million, up 17% year-over-year. Organic sales declined 5% as growth in CPI service was more than offset by continued softness in the vending and hardware markets. Antares Vision sales were impacted in the third quarter by project timing in the life sciences end market. However, our backlog and opportunity funnel remain healthy.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 2% to $71 million, with strong pricing and productivity offsetting lower organic volume flow-through. Adjusted EBITDA margin declined 430 basis points, reflecting the expected dilution from Antares Vision. We are actively deploying the Crane Business System and beginning to realize operating synergies as identified in the acquisition business case. This puts Antares Vision on track to achieve its targeted adjusted EBITDA contribution for 2026. Lastly, DTT backlog was approximately $234 million, including approximately $125 million from Antares Vision. CPI backlog remains stable. Turning to slide seven, we ended the third quarter with net leverage of approximately 2.5x and expect to meet our year-end target of approximately 2.3x, driven by our robust cash generation.

We have a strong balance sheet with no fixed-rate debt maturities until 2036, and we will continue to allocate capital through a disciplined framework focused on the highest return uses of cash and long-term shareholder value creation. Turning to slide eight, we are raising the midpoint of our adjusted EPS guidance and narrowing the range to $4.32-$4.42. For the full year, we now expect total sales growth of approximately 14%, with DTT lower and SAT modestly better than our previous midpoint guidance. In SAT, we expect total sales growth of approximately 11%, supported by strong international currency backlog and continued demand across the segment. In DTT, we expect total sales growth in the high teens.

This updated outlook reflects continued market softness in CPI vending and hardware and slower life sciences project conversion in Antares Vision. We continue to expect adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 24%, supported by pricing, productivity initiatives, and realization of acquisition synergies at Crane Authentication and Antares Vision. We now expect non-operating expenses of approximately $75 million-$80 million, reflecting lower borrowing costs. I will close with a few directional comments on 2027 and note that we will provide our complete 2027 guidance framework on the fourth quarter earnings call. In SAT, we expect continued broad-based growth, supported by sustained high demand and strong backlog conversion.

We expect to see margin accretion in SAT from higher revenue and realization of operating synergies at Crane Authentication. Within DTT, we expect continued growth in Antares Vision and in CPI service, where we are expanding our service offering to third-party equipment. We anticipate CPI hardware markets will remain soft. We will continue to mitigate the impact of lower volume with productivity initiatives, and we remain confident in our ability to drive operational improvements that will enable us to achieve EBITDA margin accretion and continued strong free cash flow generation in CPI. I will now turn the call back to Aaron to provide closing remarks.

Aaron Saak: Thanks, Christina. To wrap up, we delivered a solid third quarter. SAT continued to generate growth and margin expansion. In DTT, we continue to execute on the Antares Vision integration, and disciplined execution and productivity helped offset softness in the CPI vending and hardware markets. Over the last three years, we have repositioned Crane NXT around attractive markets supported by durable secular tailwinds, including the rise of industrialized counterfeiting and digitization of supply chains. As we continue forward, our focus is on extending our leadership in the markets we serve while continuing to optimize the portfolio to enhance growth and returns. Our proprietary technologies, strong customer relationships, and commercial wins reinforce our confidence in this strategy.

The Crane Business System remains at the core of how we will drive continuous improvement, margin expansion, and free cash flow, providing financial flexibility to deploy capital towards the highest return opportunities and create long-term shareholder value. Thank you again for joining us this morning, and again, thanks to our Crane NXT associates around the world for their continued commitment to our customers. With that, operator, we are ready to take our first question.

Operator: Thank you. At this time, we will conduct the question-and-answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, you will need to press star 11 on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. To withdraw your question, please press star 11 again. We kindly request that you limit to one question and one follow-up question. Please stand by while we compile the Q&A roster. Our first question comes from the line of Matt Summerville of D.A. Davidson. Your line is now open.

Matt Summerville: Morning. Maybe starting with Authentication and Antares, where are you in terms of EBITDA profitability run rates in those businesses relative to what you expected at the onset of the three acquisitions that you've done so far? Where can that get to in a year? Then maybe can you talk about, frame up a little bit more on the Antares funnel and backlog? Then I have a follow-up.

Aaron Saak: Hey, good morning again, Matt. Thanks for the question. Why don't I start on Antares? I'll take that question in general, then I'll hand it over to Christina for Authentication. Matt, on Antares, hey, we're seven months in post-close to the acquisition. As I said in the prepared remarks, the integration's going well, and we feel confident in the long-term growth of not only the markets, but the business and the technology that we have. So a little bit to your last part of your question as it relates to Q4, we have orders in-house, and we're building those for several important pharma customers, and they've asked for delivery in Q1.

To give you context for that, for these pharma customers, they have to stop production in their lines to install our equipment, and they're operating now at very high capacity, so they don't want to stop their lines here in Q4. So that's what's really driving the delivery and the push-out of those installs into the first of next year. Again, we feel good about where we're at in the market, the relationship with those customers, and our backlog.

So, to get to the first part of your question, with the efforts that we have underway, driving synergies and productivity, doing the Kaizens, like I mentioned with CBS, we're going to end this year on target for EBITDA in the business exactly as we expected, and we're on track for the EBITDA expansion over the coming years as we announced at the time of the close of Antares. We feel very good about that. Christina, I'm going to hand it to you for authentication.

Christina Cristiano: Great. Thanks, Aaron. In terms of authentication, performance in the third quarter was very strong, and we saw a mid-teens EBITDA margin, which is in line with our expectations, and that's really the strong operating performance of the business and also realization of the planned synergies starting to read through. As we look ahead to the, I think you mentioned one year out, but even for the full year, we'll expect that to continue. Generally, a mid-teens EBITDA margin, and if you look ahead as we go forward, the group will continue to recognize operating synergies, so we'll expect to see further accretion in the EBITDA margin as we move forward.

Matt Summerville: Got it. As a follow-up, Aaron, maybe talk a little bit about if your thinking has evolved over the last six months with respect to portfolio optimization, and in that context, how you're thinking about M&A looking ahead versus maybe other capital uses like share buybacks.

Aaron Saak: Sure. Happy to take that, Matt. I think you should expect that we are always assessing how best to optimize our portfolio, and that's to drive shareholder value. That's our goal. As we've been discussing now for some time, we're continuing to build on our capabilities as the leader in authentication and traceability technologies, and you see that again in the step of closing Antares Vision now seven months ago. As the company's getting bigger and it's growing, it's always good practice to focus on markets that are growing and areas we can play and win. In that context, we are actively assessing how best to optimize the portfolio for the long term.

As that relates more broadly to capital allocation, I just point out, the results here of third quarter matter, another proof point of our ability to generate very strong free cash flow, and that puts us in a great position for capital allocation, which I would boil down to really four priorities that have been consistent in our disciplined framework for the past several years. Number one, we're going to continue to invest in high-return organic growth investments, and you see that in SAT. Number two, we're going to continue to pay down the debt. As Christina mentioned, we're going to be in the low twos by the end of the year.

Third, we're going to continue to pay our dividend. We raised it this year. You can see by our free cash flow, we're in a very good position to do that in 2027. Then we'll look to a combination of share buybacks or M&A. Our focus right now in M&A is the integration of Antares Vision, and that's really our priority for the next several months.

Matt Summerville: Got it. Thank you, guys.

Operator: Our next question comes from the line of Bob Labick of CJS Securities. Your line is now open.

Bob Labick: Good morning. Thanks for taking our questions.

Bob Labick: Yeah. Obviously, we are super excited, and hopefully find out relatively soon about the new upgrade $10 bill and the U.S. upgrade cycle, and congratulations on the Canadian $20 bill, which seems to have an awful lot of your content on it. My question is, we know about the U.S. upgrade cycle. This is a little harder, but where generally are we in terms of an upgrade replacement cycle internationally? Can you remind us where you stand on micro-optics capacity expansion and the timing to fulfill this demand?

Aaron Saak: Hey, thanks, Bob, for that question, and good morning to you too. Overall, if I go back to SAT, just a strong quarter in performance by that team, high single-digit growth, high single-digit growth in our currency business, and just another strong quarter in our international currency business, just continues to perform well. To your question, we see sustained demand in international currency driven by our technology, not only in 2027, but beyond. As we mentioned, we are now looking at orders into 2028. That is coming from emerging markets that I would say are in the middle of their continued redesign cycles. We are seeing demand and potential demand from larger developed markets.

The best example, as you just mentioned, is the Canadian 20, a terrific marquee customer for us that really sets the precedent for the use of micro-optics in more emerging and developed markets, and it is terrific. That is why we are investing, as Christina mentioned, and we are staying ahead of this demand, so we are ready to serve our customers as that comes online. We expect the backlog in this business to remain at these sustained high levels all the way for the foreseeable future.

Bob Labick: Okay, great. Sticking with currency, the U.S. currency print order was very strong that came out in this quarter. Can you just remind us how that flows through for timing for you guys and impact on the mix of the order and how that flows through on margins in terms of looking forward in U.S. currency and SAT?

Aaron Saak: Yeah. Happy to take that, Bob. To the point you just raised, we are very pleased with the 2027 print order from the Fed. It is an increase in double digits in volume. It is a nice skew of the mix over to the $100 bill, which of course uses our micro-optic technology. This is good for the currency business. We typically operate about three or four months ahead of the print requirement for the BEP. So we will start realizing that early in 2027 as they execute their annual plan. Again, feels very good. For several quarters, we have been discussing the new $10 bill program is continuing to move along.

We expect that to come here in 2027, as we have been discussing. Our work is on the $50 bill, which is progressing. So we are really ready to go. As you mentioned for SAT, Q3 performance speaks for itself. Backlog is high. We have incredibly high visibility, not just to Q4, but to 2027, and that is giving us a lot of confidence in the business and why I am very bullish about the SAT segment. So I am going to leave it at that, Bob. I think any more details on specifics in 2027, we will leave to the Q4 call and our updated guidance.

Bob Labick: Super. That is great. Thanks very much.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Bobby Brooks of Northland Capital Markets. Your line is now open.

Bobby Brooks: Hey, good morning, team, and thank you for taking my question.

Bobby Brooks: Good morning. Looking at the 2027 currency capacity, is that kind of all accounted for at this point, or is there still ability for you guys to take on additional orders?

Christina Cristiano: Hey, Bobby. I will start on that one, and maybe if Aaron wants to chime in at the end. We, as you know, our backlog is very robust, and we are taking orders into 2028. We have got the capacity to fulfill all the orders in 2027. About 65% of our backlog will be delivered in 2027, in the backlog that sits today. As we look out past that, as we start to take orders into 2028, that is why we are adding more capacity to drive further growth in the future from 2028 and beyond. As you know, we are investing in new micro-optics production lines that will provide that capacity for the years after 2028.

Aaron Saak: Yeah. Hey, Bobby, I just reiterate what Christina said. Our confidence in this business and being able to deliver 2027 is incredibly high. You look at these U.S. prints order, which is, again, very positive, and the contract renewals that go out 10 years for us. We have secured now 160 years of being the sole provider of this technology to the U.S. government, and it feels very, very good, again, why we are so bullish on the business.

Bobby Brooks: Got it. Just a clarification, because I think in the prepared remarks, you talked about accelerating those investments in the new micro-optic production lines. What does that mean in reality?

Christina Cristiano: Yeah, thanks for that follow-up. We are actively pursuing initiatives to move forward projects so we can get that capacity online sooner, and you will start to see our CapEx pick up in the fourth quarter in the Crane Currency business. In total, our CapEx for the whole company will still be between 4% and 5% of sales, but it will be allocating more toward Crane Currency as we really want to move those growth investments forward. We are actively working on those investments. In addition, we are hiring and training people to work in the manufacturing facilities on the new production equipment.

That is what I meant by the accelerating investments, and we will have more to say about our expectations for CapEx in the February earnings call.

Aaron Saak: Yeah, I would just add, Bobby, to what Christina said. Where we have the opportunity and we are pushing here to move faster, we are going to go faster because of the high confidence we have in orders coming in, the book of business not only we have today, but what we see coming. Those are just excellent returns for our business. So where we can move faster, we are going to move. We have got the team in place, we have certainly got the balance sheet in place, and now it is just getting in and building out these sites to meet customer demand.

Bobby Brooks: Definitely. Just last one for me, wanted to hear a little bit more specific drivers of the change in the DTT organic growth outlook. I think, Christina, you mentioned CPI and CPI vending and hardware as the driver, but were not those already expected to be weak? Maybe I am off base, and correct me if I am wrong, but if not, just what occurred the last few months that weakened those verticals?

Aaron Saak: Yeah, Bobby, I will start, and I will let Christina chime in here as well. We think about CPI, and as we have been talking about it, as three businesses. First is services, and that is growing, and we are really seeing very nice growth in multi-vendor services. That is where we are going out attaching services to non-CPI equipment, and that is performing just as we expected. The second business is vending. That is coming in maybe just a little bit softer to kind of flattish growth for the year, not so different than what we talked about last quarter.

Then really where we are seeing the most headwind is inside the hardware business, and a lot of that is coming from retail, where we have seen pushouts by several big box retailers of their previously announced upgrade and refresh programs. And so we have visibility to that now as we get into Q4, and that's where we've just been prudent to adjust the guide for the rest of Q4.

Bobby Brooks: Appreciate the color. Congrats on strong quarter.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Ian Zaffino of Oppenheimer. Your line is now open.

Isaac Sellhausen: Hey, good morning. This is Isaac Sellhausen on for Ian. Appreciate you taking the questions. First

Isaac Sellhausen: Hey, good morning. Just on the EBITDA margin guidance, that was unchanged despite the lower kind of revenue outlook. Maybe if you could touch on, excuse me, touch on some of the offsets to that, like lower volume leverage, and then maybe how much comes from SAT mix or any other incremental productivity gains. Thanks.

Christina Cristiano: Yeah. Thanks for that, Isaac. So we're holding our full year EBITDA estimate in the mid-20s percent, and really based on a very strong operating performance in the businesses, and specifically in CPI, where we're mitigating the lower volumes. So you're seeing that read through. We've also got favorable mix in our Crane Currency business, which is also reading through. When you put those things together, that's how we're able to maintain that margin for the full year. In the quarter, you saw very strong margin performance, and we expect that to continue.

Isaac Sellhausen: Okay, understood. Just as a follow-up, you talked a little bit about multiple long-term commercial wins across segments. I think specific to SAT, maybe you could frame whether those represent new customers or renewals, and then kind of maybe initial ramp or timing of any of those wins. Thanks.

Aaron Saak: Yeah, Isaac. Certainly as it relates to the U.S. government wins, or call those contract renewals, that's an existing customer, but it just reinforces the moats around this business and how durable and sustainable it is. Again, these are contract renewals that go out, in some cases, for 10 years, which is just fantastic for the stability of the business. Inside the rest of SAT, it's a combination of expansion through new customers and share of wallet or redesigns with existing customers. In authentication, the example there is an existing customer, but where we've expanded with a contract and continued new technology into their portfolio.

It's really a combination of both, and I think that's what continues to give us confidence in the leadership, technology leadership that we have that's very sustainable.

Aaron Saak: Yeah, and just to be clear, Trent, you're talking about, as we talk about authentication, brand, government, and identity?

Aaron Saak: What you're Yeah. So, overall, I would say these markets are growing mid-single digits, and we feel good about our position there. Brand particularly is, I just think, at mid-single digits, and there we have a very diverse set of customers, from major sports leagues to apparel. So, a very diverse mix of clients. It tends to move kind of in general with kind of a market. It's a book-and-ship type business. Government tends to have bigger contracts. That's like our Crane Currency business, where we're selling tax stamps or other government revenue solutions.

There we have the opportunity for not only general kind of continued flow at mid-single digits, but as we win new accounts, those tend to add kind of project wins that could be a nice catalyst for us. Finally, identification security, or IDs, here again, kind of a mid-single-digit grower. What we're seeing in that business, though, is the need for new and upgraded IDs is continuing due to the rise of counterfeiting. Again, that's just back to the macro trends playing out in this business. So, across all three of these kind of end markets and verticals, how we think about authentication, we see sustained mid-single-digit growth.

Mike Halloran: Thanks. Then, as you saw the good SAT margin performance in the third quarter, maybe it would be helpful to bucket some of the reasons for that. I know you talked to them more generally, but just trying to understand what within that 29% EBITDA margin is sustainable from a run rate perspective, or if there are any benefits or one-offs on the quarter for us to note. Christina Cristiano: Yeah, I'll take that one, Saak. As you said, very strong EBITDA margin at 29%, up 60 basis points year-over-year. I think we're into a stable run rate business, and that's how I would think about it going forward into 2027.

#3250. macOS 27.3 Golden Gate public beta 1 now available, here’s everything new

Following the release of macOS 27.3 developer beta 1, Apple is now rolling out the first test build for users enrolled in the public beta. Here’s what’s coming

Contrary to macOS 27.2, it looks like Apple had quite a bit in store for macOS 27.3 and its counterparts.

In addition to expanding Siri AI to four more languages, including Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese, the system also introduces several new Safari features, including Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode for websites, and the ability to organize and manage tabs using Siri AI.

macOS 27.3 also adds native Markdown rendering to Quick Look, allowing users to preview .md files with proper formatting instead of raw Markdown syntax.

The update also expands Siri AI’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing users to perform more complex actions in apps like Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders.

Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to create advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions, allowing the assistant to coordinate multistep actions across different apps.

Users who enjoyed the wallpaper introduced with the new touchscreen MacBook Pro will also find a new screensaver called Pro Lighteensaver, which features light moving along the metallic-looking lines that form the word “PRO.”

Earlier this week, Apple also confirmed that macOS 27.3 will introduce new checks for potentially harmful content shared through public iCloud links. Starting with the update, files and photos shared using the “Anyone with the link” option will be checked by Apple, which may remove flagged content or take action against accounts that violate its policies.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 1 is 26C5035r, which is the same as the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

Did you spot anything new in today’s beta? Let us know in the comments.

#3248. Consumer Appetite for Personal AI Goes Mainstream

The November issue of IEEE Spectrum is here!

Nearly 70 percent of respondents say they want an AI assistant in their next device, according to a new report

Qualcomm builds intelligent, connected, computing and AI solutions that transform industries and advance human progress.

A recent report by Qualcomm Technologies, built on a survey of more than 12,000 people across key geographies worldwide, shows that around 70 percent of respondents express strong interest in an AI assistant that can interact naturally through voice and seamlessly manage devices, apps, and everyday tasks.

This article is brought to you by Qualcomm Technologies.

For many consumers, much of the promise and appeal of AI is personal. Consumers are looking past generic tools and want to know how these technologies will help them in their daily lives. These trends coincide with the advent of new classes of wearable devices that, in addition to being able to leverage powerful frontier models, feature built-in intelligence that understand the context of a user. Where are they? What are they seeing and hearing? What are their habits, their preferences, their schedules?

It’s an astonishing pivot, from passive accessories that served mostly to send users smartphone notifications to proactive, intelligent companions. The smartphone is no longer the center of that universe; though it’s still incredibly important, in this personal AI paradigm, the AI is the UI. And it shifts the focus toward you, the user.

These new technologies are exciting. But what do consumers really want?

A Personal AI report, commissioned by Qualcomm Technologies, built on a survey of more than 12,000 people across key geographies worldwide (the U.S., U.K., Germany, India, Brazil, and China) focused on the rise of personal AI in intelligent wearables looks deeply at these developments.

The smartphone is no longer the center of that universe; though it’s still incredibly important, in this personal AI paradigm, the AI is the UI.

Survey respondents are less interested in single devices and are responding more to the idea of connected ecosystems. As people expand their roster of devices, it only makes sense. Instead of relying entirely on a smartphone and a laptop, respondents also have connected technology in their cars, as well as intelligent wearables like smartwatches, smart glasses, hearables, and other wearables like rings, pins, and pendants. They want those devices to work in concert, and the way to do that is to decentralize any single one of them. Instead, the AI agent that knows the user and works across all of those devices becomes the unifying factor.

Consider a typical workday: A user’s watch detects it is time to leave for a meeting and, with permission, their AI agent factors in calendar details, real-time traffic and battery status across their devices. In the car, it suggests the best route and briefs them on their meeting agenda. As they arrive, smart glasses surface a discreet reminder, such as the meeting location or the name of a new contact, while the phone stays in their pocket. No one device has to do everything; each plays the role it is best suited for, coordinated by a personal AI agent that understands the user’s context and acts only at the user’s direction.

With this in mind, simply adding more hardware to the mix isn’t sufficient. Even though respondents will be open to new form factors, they’ll demand more from their ecosystem of devices. They’ll be sensitive to points of friction and needless complexity, and they’ll require each new device to bring something new to the table — “incremental intelligence, convenience, or contextual awareness that their existing devices cannot deliver on their own what the report,” reads the report.

The usage trends are up. The report found that those who own wearables are already using AI frequently (60 percent use it at least weekly), which indicates that it’s becoming less of a fun experiment for early adopters and more of a critical mass habit.

The “always-on” nature of intelligent wearables appears to be winning respondents, too. The report found the following statistics on average continuous wear among users:

But for all the excitement and engagement around intelligent wearables, there’s a gating factor: trust. As use cases for intelligent wearables expands to more personal and persistent experiences, trust is a necessity for Personal AI.

Notably, the report found that respondents expressed more interest in adopting intelligent wearables when Snapdragon was introduced as the enabling platform. This reinforces the value of having an established, trusted technology foundation in the mix.

The report shows that consumer appetite for AI is high, with 60-70 percent of those surveyed expressing interest in advanced AI as they consider a new device. That’s a constant. But remaining purchase drivers differed between device categories.

Audio playback quality is the most influential purchase driver for true wireless earbuds and headphones. For smartwatches, it’s display quality and responsiveness. Respondents are less concerned about technical specifications than aesthetics like materials and finish when it comes to devices like smart rings and pendants. And for smart glasses, it’s all about the type of control, whether it’s voice, gesture, or touch.

Artificial intelligence is entering a new phase, one that is deeply personal, continuously present, and seamlessly embedded into the devices we wear every day. This evolution, which we define as “Personal AI”, represents a shift away from generic, cloud-only intelligence toward AI that understands individuals in context: their habits, preferences, environments, and intent, in real time.

Alongside these purchase drivers is another key finding: Consumer appetite for Personal AI agents has gone mainstream. The report says that 70 percent of respondents “express strong interest in an AI assistant that can interact naturally through voice and seamlessly manage devices, apps, and everyday tasks.” With each individual as the center of their own ecosystem, voice becomes the most critical, natural method for interacting with agents.

Intelligent wearables comprise much of the hardware of this “ecosystem of you.” Consumers are interested in ecosystems instead of single devices, and they’re looking for agentic AI capabilities that understand and act on their behalf.

Yet so much of the industry remains undefined. OEMs and technology makers have an enormous opportunity right now to innovate and iterate on the strong technological foundations that platform makers are building. And the roadmap for what consumers want is clear.

All percentages, consumer behaviors, and attitudes stated in this report are based only on the responses of the individuals who participated in our survey.

Qualcomm Technologies is a global leader in communications and computing technologies, including leading-edge AI, high-performance, low-power computing, and connectivity solutions. Headquartered in San Diego, Calif., the company develops technologies for next-generation mobile networks and smart devices, and designs semiconductors such as mobile processors and AI chips.

The bias is deafening. Qualcomm, a chip manufacturer that is all in on AI, makes a survey and then states they found everyone loves using AI, the very AI that will run on Qualcomm chips. Clearly they don't have a conflict of interest in this. /s

#3247. Park Hotels & Resorts (PK) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Full-year guidance rose as the reopened Royal Palm South Beach ramps up.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Park Hotels & Resorts Inc. (PK -8.31%) reported a net loss of $15 million for the third quarter, while comparable RevPAR increased 8.4% to $201.02. Management reported that broad-based strength in group and leisure demand drove performance, particularly in urban markets like Washington DC, Chicago, and Boston. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for RevPAR, Adjusted EBITDA, and Adjusted FFO per share following results that exceeded internal expectations. Strategic capital allocation efforts included the reopening of the Royal Palm South Beach following a $110 million renovation and the commencement of a $100 million project at the Hilton Hawaiian Village. Management also continued its noncore disposition strategy, completing the sale of the W Chicago – City Center for $19 million in October 2026.

Operator: Greetings, and welcome to the Park Hotels and Resorts Third Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. A question-and-answer session will follow the formal presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. It is now my pleasure to introduce Ian C. Weissman, Senior Vice President, Corporate Strategy. Please go ahead.

Ian C. Weissman: Thank you, operator, and welcome, everyone, to the Park Hotels and Resorts Third Quarter 26 Earnings Call. Before we begin, I would like to remind everyone that many of the comments made today are considered forward looking statements under federal securities laws. As described in our filings with the SEC, these statements are subject to numerous risks and uncertainties that could cause future results to differ from those expressed and we are not obligated to publicly update or revise these forward looking statements. Actual performance, outcomes and results may differ materially from those expressed in forward looking statements.

Please refer to the documents filed by Park with the SEC specifically the most recent reports on Forms 10 ks and 10 Q, which identify from those contained in the forward looking statements. In addition, on today's call, we will discuss certain non GAAP financial information such as adjusted FFO, and adjusted EBITDA. You can find this information together with reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure in yesterday's earnings call as well in our 8 ks filed with the SEC the supplemental financial information available on our website at pkhotelsandresorts.com. Additionally, unless otherwise stated, all operating results will be presented on a comparable hotel basis.

This morning, Tom Baltimore, our Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, will provide an update on our strategic initiatives and review Park's third quarter performance and outlook for the year. While Sean Dell'Orto, our Chief Financial Officer, and Chief Operating Officer will provide updates on our capital investments and additional color on guidance. Following our prepared remarks, we will open the call for questions. With that, I would like to turn the call over to Tom.

Thomas Jeremiah Baltimore Jr.: Thank you, Ian and welcome, everyone. I am pleased to report that Park delivered another outstanding quarter with results meaningfully exceeding our expectations. RevPAR increased 8.4% year over year with growth accelerating from 9% in July to more than 13% in September. Despite weather related disruptions in Hawaii during August, and September. Results reflected broad based strength across the portfolio, supported by continued momentum in group, leisure, and higher rated business transient demand. RevPAR increased nearly 7% across both our resort and urban hotels. While our airport and suburban hotels grew approximately 20%, 14%, respectively. Turning to our major markets. Hawaii continues to be 1 of the most compelling growth opportunities in our portfolio.

RevPAR across our 2 resorts increased an impressive 7% despite the temporary disruption from 3 hurricanes which we estimate reduced combined RevPAR growth for the 2 resorts by nearly 280-basis-points during the quarter. Demand rebounded as conditions improved with September representing the strongest month of the quarter and RevPAR across our Hawaii resorts increased nearly 14%. Group was the primary driver of performance at both hotels in the third quarter with group rooms revenue more than doubling year over year. Which helped to drive a 110% increase in banquet and catering revenue. At Hilton Hawaiian Village, RevPAR increased 5% during the quarter. With occupancy reaching nearly 90% allowing for compression to drive stronger rates.

Particularly in September when average daily rate increased approximately 9% compared to last year. The resort also continued to gain market share achieving a RevPAR index of 105% for the quarter up 4 points from last year with gains across both occupancy and rate. Importantly, the index remains nearly 14 points below its 2021. The resort's renovated outlets and enhanced programming also helped drive record third quarter food and beverage performance with banquet and catering outlet revenue each growing 14% year-over-year. Orlando also delivered another strong quarter. With RevPAR increasing more than 5% led by continued outperformance at Bonnet Creek. The complex delivered another record breaking quarter generating its highest third quarter revenue ever.

Transient revenue increased nearly 19% year-over-year supported by premium rated luxury demand at the Waldorf. Further underscoring the exceptional quality of these properties Signia by Hilton, Orlando Bonnet Creek, and Waldorf Astoria Orlando, were recently ranked the number 2 and number 3 resorts in Orlando respectively, and Conde Nast Travelers 2026 Reader's Choice Awards. Bonnet Creek's continued strength following our significant investment demonstrates how targeted capital can elevate an asset strengthen its competitive positioning, and drive sustained earnings growth. EBITDA of the complex has grown from approximately $60 million to a level we expect to exceed $108 million this year. And we believe there is further upside as the complex continues to gain market share.

Our urban portfolio was another important source of strength. Led by Washington DC, Chicago, and Boston. Across our 2 DC Metro hotels, RevPAR increased by nearly 33% year-over-year. Supported by a 9-point increase in occupancy, and ADR growth of 16%. Group room nights increased 139% creating meaningful compression and supporting transient ADR growth of more than 17%. At our Hilton Chicago hotel, RevPAR increased more than 15% benefiting from a particularly strong citywide and event calendar and excellent transient pricing. Boston also delivered strong results. With portfolio RevPAR increasing approximately 13% supported by meaningful ADR growth, strong citywide demand, and high occupancy.

Finally, we are very excited about the early progress at Royal Palm South Beach following its approximately $110 million transformational renovation. The hotel welcomed its first guest in late July, making the third quarter very much a ramp up period. Even at this early stage, rate performance has been very encouraging with third quarter ADR of approximately $244, up nearly $60, and more than 30% above the comparable period in 2024, with September increasing to $264 or over 40% better than pre renovation results.

The team has also been focused on building awareness of the reimagined hotel posting leading travel media, Marriott sales leaders from around the world, and key industry groups, while benefiting from broad support from Marriott and our operating partners. Looking ahead, the demand backdrop is encouraging with 8 citywide events scheduled for Miami Beach in the fourth quarter. Expected to generate approximately 56 thousand room nights, up 70% compared to last year. We are also seeing strong early validation of the hotel's repositioning across both group and food and beverage. At the end of the third quarter, 2027 group revenue on the books totaled approximately $3.9 million already matching the comparable pace for 2024 the hotel's best year.

With an average daily rate, that is a $136 higher, or up nearly 40%. During the third quarter alone, the hotel booked more than 8 thousand future group room nights at $461 average daily rate, representing approximately $3.7 million of rooms revenue more than triple the amount booked during the same period in 2024. Banquet and catering has also been particularly strong. Booking nearly $1.7 million during the third quarter versus less than $200 thousand booked during the same period in 2024. Together, these early results demonstrate the opportunity to drive significantly higher rates and meaningfully higher total revenue across the property.

These results also reinforce our confidence that Royal Palm will become a meaningful contributor to Park's earnings growth over the next couple of years. On the capital allocation front, we continue to make meaningful progress executing on our noncore disposition strategy. In October, we completed the sale of the W Chicago – City Center, a 520-room hotel in Chicago for $19 million. The hotel was expected to generate an operating loss of approximately $1.3 million in 2026, with a forecasted loss of approximately $1.3 million in the fourth quarter. Making the sale immediately accretive to earnings while further enhancing the quality of our portfolio.

Our remaining noncore hotels now represent 3% to 4% of total portfolio value, and we remain committed to further reducing that exposure by year end. With active work streams on a number of assets underway. We are extremely pleased with our progress since launching the strategy late last year Of the 19 hotels originally identified as noncore, we have sold or otherwise disposed of 11 hotels, generating approximately $220 million in gross proceeds at an average multiple of more than 16x EBITDA. These transactions have reduced our exposure to lower growth assets and enabled us to focus our capital and resources on our highest quality hotels and markets.

The result is a higher quality portfolio with stronger margins, a better growth profile, and greater long term earnings potential. We believe this transformation has positioned Park to deliver sustained earnings growth and create long term shareholder value. As we look at the balance of the year, and into 2027, I remain encouraged by the strength across our portfolio. Despite continued geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty, The US economy and consumer remain resilient, healthy business activity and investment, including significant spending related to AI, should continue to support lodging demand, while historically low levels of new hotel supply provide a favorable backdrop for continued pricing power.

Against this backdrop, we expect to finish the year strong and enter 2027 with considerable momentum. Core group revenue pace is up nearly 6% and we have several distinct growth drivers. Including our recently completed capital investments, which are expected to provide meaningful embedded earnings growth. In Miami, 2027 will mark its first full year of operations at the Transformed Royal Palm South Beach. Early performance continues to reinforce our high confidence in the hotel's ramp toward approximately $28 million of stabilized hotel adjusted EBITDA by 2028 compared with approximately $3 million expected this year.

For 2027, we currently expect earnings to at least return to pre levels of approximately $14 million of EBITDA with Royal Palm alone expected to contribute approximately 200 basis points to total portfolio RevPAR growth. Hawaii represents another substantial opportunity. But the Ali'i Tower renovation expected to be completed in early 27, We will have invested approximately $350 million to strengthen the competitive positioning of our 2 resorts. With the major renovation activity behind us, solid group pace already on the books, and significant upside from recovering market share we believe our Hawaii portfolio is well positioned to continue closing the approximately $60 million EBITDA gap to its 2023 peak earnings over the next few years.

As a result, I believe Park is uniquely positioned to deliver outsized earnings growth over the next several years We have strengthened the portfolio through disciplined capital allocation, and active capital recycling, invested substantially in our highest return opportunities, and enhanced our financial flexibility through proactive balance sheet management. We are now positioned to realize the earnings benefits of that work creating a compelling path to higher EBITDA and meaningful long term value creation for our shareholders. And with that, I will turn the call over to Sean.

Sean Dell'Orto: Thanks, Tom. Overall, we were very pleased with our third quarter results. Which once again exceeded expectations with RevPAR increasing 8.4% to $201 and hotel adjusted EBITDA increasing 8% year-over-year, with hotel adjusted EBITDA margin expanding by 50 basis points to 25.7%. Adjusted EBITDA was $135 million for the quarter while adjusted FFO per share was $0.39, an increase of over 11%. We were also pleased to see broad based strength across the portfolio. Group rooms revenue increased more than 18%, while transient revenue grew over 5%, reflecting healthy demand across multiple customer segments. RevPAR growth was also well balanced, with occupancy increasing 2.4 percentage points and ADR up 5%.

Expenses increased 5% during the quarter compared with just under 4% in the first half of the year. With the reopening of the Royal Palm adding roughly 85 basis points of operating expense growth versus prior year. Excluding Royal Palm, cost per occupied room increased 3.7% in the quarter including an approximately 80-basis point impact from increased utility cost pressures. Which combined with higher occupancy and along with revenue based variable costs drove the expense growth for the quarter. But partially offset by a reduction in fixed costs mostly due to lower property insurance premiums from our annual policy renewal this past June.

Turning to capital investments, During the third quarter, we invested a total of $57 million in capital improvements, with full year CapEx expected to range between $270 million to $280 million In Hawaii, we commenced a comprehensive renovation of a 348-room Ali'i Tower Hilton Hawaiian Village in August. A $100 million project that includes a complete renovation of all guest rooms plus the addition of 3 guest rooms within the premium oceanfront tower. And enhancements to food and beverage outlets including the Tropics Bar and Grill, and 80% of the guest rooms across to nearly 3 thousand-room resort have been fully renovated.

And finally, in New Orleans, we commenced third and final phase of the main tower guest room renovation in May. Encompassing the remaining 489 guest rooms and expect the project to be completed by mid November. Upon completion, all 1.6 thousand-plus guest rooms then fully renovated, significantly enhancing the quality and competitiveness of 1 of our most important convention oriented assets. Turning to the balance sheet, we ended the third quarter with net debt of approximately $3.7 billion, translating to a trailing 12 month net debt to EBITDA ratio of just under 6x. A reduction of 0.2 of a turn since the beginning of the year.

Liquidity was $1.3 billion, including $295 million in cash and $1 billion of available capacity under our revolver. In September, we fully repaid the $1.275 billion CMBS loans secured by the Hilton Hawaiian Village Resort. Using the remaining $600 million of capacity under our delayed draw term loan together with proceeds from the $700 million delayed draw mortgage loan, secured by the Bonnet Creek complex. This transaction meaningfully extended our debt maturities by roughly 1.5 years. And we now have no significant maturities until Q4 of 28. We also finalized terms on a $205 million refinancing of Hilton Santa Barbara resort. Which will be used to repay the existing $150 million mortgage maturing in December.

And provide for future funding advances towards the property's comprehensive renovation currently planned for late 28. We expect to close this refinancing by the end of this month. With respect to our dividend, on October 15, we paid our third quarter cash dividend of $0.25 per share and on October 29, the Board approved a fourth quarter cash dividend of $0.25 per share to be paid on January 15, to stockholders of record as of December 31. The dividend currently translates to an annualized yield of approximately 6% based on recent trading levels.

Turning to guidance, following another stronger than expected quarter, we are increasing both our RevPAR and earnings guidance ranges to reflect our third quarter results and our updated expectations for the fourth quarter. Accordingly, we are raising our full year RevPAR outlook by 200 basis points at the midpoint to a new range of 5.5% to 6%. Which implies a fourth quarter growth rate between 5.5% to 7.5%. This updated outlook reflects the nearly 400 basis points of outperformance delivered during the third quarter as well as stronger than anticipated results at the start of the fourth quarter with preliminary October RevPAR increasing nearly 11%.

Driven by a 120-basis-point lift from Miami, coupled with double digit gains at Bonnet Creek, Key West, and Washington DC. From an earnings perspective, we are increasing adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $13 million at the midpoint to a new range of $635 million to $645 million while adjusted FFO guidance increases by approximately $0.08 per share at the midpoint to a new range of $2.00 to $2.05 per share. This increase to guidance also reflects an assumed annual increase in expenses of approximately 4.5% year-over-year, and 5.5% to 6.5% for the fourth quarter. With an approximate 150-basis-point impact from the reopening of Royal Palm.

Expenses are being driven by the stronger demand environment and higher occupancy expectations across the portfolio driving increases in variable costs such as labor and utilities. In addition, with respect to Royal Palm, expect fourth quarter hotel adjusted EBITDA at the property to be approximately $4 million, with full year EBITDA of approximately $3 million We very much look forward to welcoming many of you to the property next week when we host an investor tour and showcase the exceptional transformation firsthand.

The hope for a hole-free design is now hanging by a thread

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There's already been lots of rumors about how Apple will redesign the iPhone 20 and commemorate the 20th anniversary of the original iPhone's release. One of the most prominent rumors claims that the device could feature an all-glass design, with no cutouts or notches for the camera and Face ID hardware.

However, according to leaker Digital Chat Station, the iPhone 20's display will indeed feature holes for the Dynamic Island. He doesn't go into much detail about this particular design feature, but it's not all that surprising now that we've seen the iPhone Duo.

The rumors had claimed the iPhone 20 would hide the camera and Face ID beneath the screen, enabling the first truly full-screen iPhone experience. This was expected to tie into the curved glass design, which was rumored to include curved edges to simulate the appearance of a glass phone.

Of course, a Dynamic Island cutout means that illusion isn't going to be quite so convincing. You can't claim "all-glass" when there's an obvious hole at the top of the screen.

Of course, the problem with under-display camera technology is that the screen is in the way. Apple has made some headway: The iPhone Duo has an under-display FaceTime camera, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max moved Face ID's IR camera beneath the screen.

But the Duo's FaceTime camera is not great — with a resolution of 4 megapixels — and it certainly isn't the kind of camera you'd want to take selfies with. That's a common problem with under-display cameras, and it seems even Apple hasn't been able to figure out how to compensate for it.

Obviously, the Duo already has a 12MP front camera, as well as the ability to shoot selfies by combining the rear cameras with the outer display — so it's not a huge loss. But since the iPhone 20 won't be able to do any of those things, it seems unlikely that an under-display camera will be up to scratch.

This is a disappointing leak, and while there's no telling how things may actually pan out over the next several months, it makes sense that the iPhone 20 will keep the Dynamic Island around. The only question I have is whether the Dynamic Island will stay the same size, or if Apple will manage to trim it down even more.

Are you excited for a near all-glass iPhone 20? Sound off in the comments.

#3243. Multiphysics Modeling for Next-Generation Electromagnetic Manufacturing Technologies



Advances in sensing, manufacturing, computational resources, and data-driven methods are enabling new approaches to electromagnetic sensing, non-destructive evaluation, and advanced materials processing. This webinar will demonstrate how the COMSOL Multiphysics software supports predictive modeling by coupling electromagnetic fields with thermal, chemical, mechanical, and transport phenomena across multiple length and time scales.

The first application we will show focuses on eddy-current thermometry for reconstructing three-dimensional temperature fields in metal plates. Temperature-dependent electrical conductivity alters induced currents and magnetic fields, enabling volumetric thermal inference. COMSOL simulations of defects and laser-induced transient heating will support validation of reconstruction algorithms. Multifrequency excitation will be investigated to improve depth discrimination through frequency-dependent penetration depths and sensitivities.

The second application examines microwave-enabled volumetric additive manufacturing of ceramic components. A high-power microwave beamforming array delivers localized energy into three-dimensional volumes, enabling processing of opaque, particle-laden resins. Coupled COMSOL models of electromagnetic propagation, microwave absorption, heat transfer, and ceramic sintering kinetics are used to predict temperature evolution, reaction progression, spatial resolution, and processing scalability. Future extensions will incorporate pulsed excitation, fluid flow, resin viscosity, convection, shrinkage, and solid mechanics.

Together, these examples demonstrate how the COMSOL software can integrate multiphysics modeling with sensing, manufacturing, and data inversion. This webinar will present two applications of coupled electromagnetic and thermal modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics: eddy-current thermometry in metal plates and microwave-assisted processing of ceramic-loaded resins. By connecting simulation with practical engineering systems, COMSOL-based modeling can accelerate technology development, reduce experimental iteration, and support reliable scale-up of next-generation electromagnetic technologies.

#3242. Report: Apple’s planned $7 billion bond sale attracts four times as much demand

Apple has filed a preliminary prospectus with the SEC outlining plans to issue seven series of bonds. Here are the details.

Over the past week, several Big Tech companies have turned to the bond market to raise billions of dollars amid growing investments in AI infrastructure.

Meta, for instance, just raised $15 billion through a US bond offering, followed by another €9 billion (roughly $10 billion) in European bonds. Earlier this week, Alphabet raised €6 billion (approximately $6.7 billion), while Microsoft completed a $25 billion bond sale last week, its first since 2017.

Apple has also turned to bond sales in the past to raise billions of dollars.

Previous offerings include those in 2015, 2019, 2020, and 2021. Most recently, Apple raised $4.5 billion through a four-part bond offering in May 2025, which attracted approximately $10 billion in investor orders.

Earlier today, Apple filed a preliminary prospectus with the SEC outlining plans to issue seven series of bonds maturing between 2028 and 2036.

However, while other Big Tech companies have been borrowing heavily amid growing AI infrastructure investments, Apple’s filing makes no specific mention of AI.

Instead, the company says it intends to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, potentially including stock buybacks, dividends, acquisitions, and debt repayment, as it has done in previous bond offerings.

And while the prospectus didn’t specify how much Apple intends to raise, Bloomberg reported soon after that the company is targeting approximately $7 billion, with investors already placing orders totaling around $31 billion.

According to Bloomberg, strong investor demand has also helped Apple secure more favorable borrowing terms, with investors willing to accept lower interest rates than those offered by Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle in their recent bond sales.

All of this is happening amid a massive tech sell-off, which saw the Nasdaq 100 plunge more than 6% at one point today, with Nvidia shares falling about 8% and the S&P 500 dropping nearly 4%.

Apple’s own stock is also taking a hit, trading down 1.49% at the time of publication, but it is faring better than those of its Big Tech peers, whose stocks have become more closely tied to the AI spending boom.

Be that as it may, Apple is expected to finalize the size and pricing of its bond offering soon, potentially as early as later today, after which the company will file the definitive terms with the SEC.

Today, Motorola has shared a whole lot more info on its brand-new Signature 27 — packing the new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 I tested and a retina-searing 12,000-nit display. But not only will it test your eyes, it will test the limits of your wallet.

This is a $1,599 phone. Yowzers. Pre-sales will go live on November 16.

Motorola, the company that has spent the last decade charming us with accessible mid-range and affordable phones, has jumped straight into the ultra-flagship pool. And to justify this phone compared to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, it built a device with a spec sheet that's absurdly overpowered.

If you’re going to charge $1,600 for a slab phone in this economy, you have to throw the kitchen sink at it. Turns out Motorola chucked the entire plumbing system in there for good measure — packing it all into a rather suave, slimline design.

Let’s start with the screen — a 1.5K Extreme AMOLED Duo tandem display that peaks at a bonkers 12,000 nits of brightness. For context, Motorola says users can “comfortably view” this “on a sunny afternoon,” but it’s closer to being able to read a map on the surface of the sun.

And for when you do want to flashbang your eyeballs with TikTok, there’s Bang & Olufsen-tuned speakers, too!

Under the hood is that Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, which as you know from my testing is an absolute monster. This is kept from melting your hands by an ArcticMesh cooling system with a massive vapor chamber.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

And to keep that silicon running, Motorola’s crammed in a gargantuan 7,000 mAh silicon-carbon battery that supports 90W wired charging and 50W wireless charging.

To further justify that astronomical price tag, Motorola strapped a camera block to the back of the phone that is bordering on clinical insanity. I’ll be real with you, it does look a bit weird to me. But I promise it’s functions are crazy.

The main shooter is a 50MP Sony sensor with a massive f/1.6 aperture designed to suck in as much light as physically possible. Next to it is a 50MP ultrawide, but the real flex is the 200MP periscope sensor capable of 100x Super Zoom Pro.

Need to take a selfie? That’s also a 50MP sensor, capable of shooting full 4K video.

But the wildest addition in my eyes is the industry’s first dedicated EVS “Action Sensor.” It’s not a camera; it’s a dedicated piece of hardware whose sole job is to detect pixel-level light intensity changes to freeze fast-moving subjects without blurring. Think of it like the equivalent of having a super fast shutter speed — something that’s a rarity in smartphones.

Pair that with Dolby Vision support and an AI video enhancement engine that optimizes dynamic range in real-time, and you effectively have a full camera rig in your pocket.

The Signature 27 is explicitly designed to run Gemini Intelligence and the brand’s own Qira AI ecosystem. To run the multi-step AI agents locally, Motorola needed to boost the RAM, which they’ve done in a rather clever way.

In silicon, you’ve got up to 16GB LPDDR5X, but with the RAM boost feature, that can be scaled up to a staggering 24GB of memory — utilizing some of the on-board storage.

This paves the way to a clever hybrid system where Gemini handles the super complex generative stuff, but local model work is entirely possible too. However, it does explain why the retail price has been driven into the stratosphere.

The Motorola Signature 27 is looking set to be a gorgeous, hyper-capable device that will likely outspec almost everything else released.

But it is also a 12,000-nit warning sign. Between Apple’s price hikes and Motorola’s $1,599 super slab, the era of an “affordable flagship killer” is behind us. If you want top-tier specs in this market, there’s quite the premium to pay.
